title: Stellar vault: `cancel_change` lets the freezer cancel its own replacement (u32 kind narrowed with `as u8`)
description:
Soroban contract functions cannot take a `u8`, so the Stellar vault's `apply_change` and `cancel_change` take `kind: u32` (lib.rs:292, 297; messages.rs:436, 487). The guard that must stop the freezer from cancelling its own replacement compares the full u32 (`require(env, kind != FREEZER_CHANGE as u32, VaultError::NotFreezer)`, messages.rs:490), but the lookup that picks the pending slot then truncates it: `pending()` does `match kind as u8 { CAP_UPDATE => .., FREEZER_CHANGE => &mut cfg.pending_freezer, .. }` (messages.rs:498-505), and `apply_change` does `match kind as u8` again (messages.rs:454). `263u32 as u8 == 7 == FREEZER_CHANGE`, so `cancel_change(263)` passes the guard (263 != 7), resolves to `pending_freezer`, and clears it (messages.rs:491-495). The twins (NEAR, Solana) take `kind: u8`, so the aliasing exists only here; no test passes a kind above 255 (tests/vault.rs:556 only tries 7).
Scenario (VLT-2/VLT-5 recovery path broken): the freezer account key is compromised or the guardian turns hostile. It calls `freeze()` (14 days, renewable before expiry); while frozen `pay_owed` pays 0, `deposit`/`refund` revert and every `apply_change` except the freezer's own replacement is held. The owner proposes FREEZER_CHANGE on the factory (GUARDIAN_DELAY 7 days), anyone delivers it (deliver has no freeze check), it queues for GOVERNANCE_DELAY 7 days; the hostile freezer signs `cancel_change(263)` and the pending replacement vanishes (the nonce mark stays at that message's nonce, so the factory must send a fresh message, wait another 14 days in total, and the freezer cancels again). VERIFIER_ROTATION is also held by the freeze and cancellable. Result: every index's XLM and every failed-intake deposit on the vault stays locked for as long as the freezer keeps refreezing; the only exit left is to let the checkpoint stall (7 days) and wait for the 180-day snapshot exit, which keepers would have to choose deliberately. This breaks the stated rule (AGENTS.md: 'the freezer may cancel a waiting raise or rotation, never its own replacement'; README; spec VLT-2) which exists precisely to bound a hostile freezer. Traced end to end in the source, not run (no Soroban toolchain here). Preconditions: freezer key compromised/malicious (a trusted-but-bounded role). Side effects of the same cast: `ChangeApplied`/`ChangeCancelled` events carry the unnormalised kind (e.g. 263) so indexers misreport.
priorArt: VLT-2 (freezer may not block its own replacement) regressed on the Stellar twin; VLT-5; SOL-3 twin rule in AGENTS.md

title: The owner can freeze every vault's payouts at once and renew the freeze forever, though the docs give the freeze to the guardian and say an owner compromise costs nothing
description:
`freezeChain` is `onlyOwnerOrGuardian` (HybridIndexFactory.sol:113-116). It has no delay, no veto and no rate limit, and it always emits `FREEZE` (L132). On the vault, `FREEZE` needs only one proof and no checkpoint coverage (`_needsBoth` returns false, XindexVault.sol:398-399, so the VLT-3 gate at L228 is skipped), skips the nonce check (L289-292), and sets `frozenUntil = now + 14 days` (L571-575). While the vault is frozen: `_release` pays 0 (L440-441), so every BURN, MIGRATE and snapshot claim stays owed; `refund` reverts (L534); `deposit` reverts (L178); and `applyChange` reverts for every key but the freezer's (L322). Nothing can unfreeze the vault. The owner cannot be removed (`renounceOwnership` reverts, IndexFactory.sol:442, and only the owner can transfer ownership). Checkpoints keep advancing, so the vault never stalls and the snapshot exit (L673-677) never opens.

Scenario: a hostile or compromised owner Safe calls `freezeChain(X)` every 13 days and delivers each FREEZE with one proof, which it can do itself. Holders of every index holding X's coin can still `redeem` the Ethereum legs, but every vault leg stays owed indefinitely, and mints on X stop for every index. Nothing is stolen, but all vault-held value on X is held hostage with no end. The owner can also seat a freezer of its own (`proposeFreezer`, 7 + 7 days), whose `freeze()` is equally unlimited.

The docs promise otherwise:
- AGENTS.md:196-205 lists the owner's powers without `freezeChain` and says "There is no pause".
- README.md:96 says no admin can pause an index.
- Design 2026-09-29: §3.1 gives the freeze to the guardian only ("expires by itself"), and the decision row at L785 reads "No pause -> Guardian freeze, expiring".
- Design §8.1 row L620 says an owner compromise means "0 immediately; holders exit within 30 days".
- ARCHITECTURE.md:917-918 bounds an owner compromise by the 30-day rotations only.

The Stage B spec (5.2, L267) does give the freeze to "the owner or guardian", without marking it as a deviation from the design. BNB-I2 documented only the guardian's version, bounded by its replacement plus 14 days. The owner's version has no bound.
priorArt: BNB-I2 (guardian only, bounded by replacement), DA-12 (the guardian's rebalance stall)

title: Since LG-4, a one-day gap in P1 or P2 proving manufactures a stall that only RECOVERY_PROPOSER can end, with holders locked out meanwhile
description: Design 6.9 (design/2026-09-29-v4-hybrid-architecture.md 506-508), spec 5.6 (line 537) and AGENTS.md 430-431 all rest the owner's stall-recovery power on one premise: 'anyone can keep a vault's checkpoints current, so nobody (the owner included) can manufacture a stall'. LG-4's fix broke the premise. FinalityVerifier.update (86-98) refuses every proof once lagEnds() = GENESIS_TIME + anchorEpoch*384 + 1 day (101-103) has passed, and nothing else can ever move the anchor, so a verifier that receives no proof for ~24h is dead for good. Then: (1) advanceCheckpoint (586-601) can only reach the last block the dead verifier's recorded ranges cover (_agreed -> verifyCheckpoint -> _checkHeader needs a range), so stalled() (604-606) becomes true 7 days after that block's timestamp; (2) nothing can rotate the pair: VERIFIER_ROTATION needs both proofs of a log at or before the checkpoint (deliver 224-230), and any rotation the factory emits after the death sits in an uncovered block; (3) nobody can lapse a successor, since only a non-stale advance does (594-600) and the dead pair can never prove a recent block. The only exits are proposeSuccessor (614-640, RECOVERY_PROPOSER only, whose continuity test runs the proposer's own verifier code, VLT-I1) and the snapshot exit 187 days in. Throughout, every BURN sent after the last covered block reverts NotCheckpointed (228-230), so holders cannot leave that chain. Scenario (hostile or compromised owner Safe, the 'owner Safe compromised' row the design considers): the owner's operators are the only ones running the SP1 and RISC Zero provers (no proof has been generated by anyone yet, spec 10), and they stop submitting for a day. P1/P2 die; 7 days later the vault stalls; RECOVERY_PROPOSER proposes a pair it controls; the freezer vetoes twice (vetoSuccessor 643-651), the third is adopted after 30 days (adoptSuccessor 654-670, callable by anyone; a freeze does not hold it). The freezer cannot be replaced during the stall (FREEZER_CHANGE is loosening, so it waits for a checkpoint). After adoption the pair proves forged BURN/MIGRATE within the speed limit, a forged FREEZER_CHANGE the freezer can neither cancel (cancelChange 331) nor hold with a freeze (applyChange 322), then a floor raise its own freezer will not cancel: the whole chain's coins are gone in about four months, during none of which could a holder exit there. Through the normal path (30-day ROTATION_DELAY on Ethereum, guardian cancel) holders can exit while the rotation is public; the stall path removes that. Before LG-4 anyone could revive the old pair from an old anchor, ending the stall and lapsing a hostile successor permissionlessly; the fix made the owner's recovery power gated only by third-party proving liveness, and AGENTS.md 437 now lists LG-4 under the very bullet that says a stall cannot be manufactured. The same holds on the twins that share the lag rule (Solana, NEAR, Stellar, Sui, Aptos). Related: A4-02 (an honest successor cannot pass the continuity test at all).
proposedFix: (a) Correct the premise everywhere it is stated, and make independent provers an explicit requirement. AGENTS.md 430-431: before: '- **A stall is only ever Ethereum's formats breaking.** Anyone can advance a vault's checkpoint while P1 and P2 work, so\n  a stall (7 days without one) cannot be manufactured. Only then may the owner's emergency multisig propose a' after: '- **A stall comes from Ethereum's formats breaking, or from a day without a P1 or P2 update.** P1 and P2 stop for good a day behind (LG-4), so a day in which nobody submits a proof of either system stalls every vault it serves a week later, and from then only the owner's emergency multisig, or the snapshot exit, ends it: provers independent of the owner must update both daily. Only in a stall may the owner's emergency multisig propose a'. Same change to spec design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-b-spec.md 537 and design/2026-09-29-v4-hybrid-architecture.md 506-508, and a README known limitation beside 551-553. (b) Code option (owner's call): a lag death is not a format break, so do not let it hand the owner recovery: add 'function lagEnds() external view returns (uint256);' to IEthereumEventVerifier, and in XindexVault.vetoSuccessor (643-651) replace 'if (count >= MAX_RECOVERY_VETOES) revert VetoesExhausted();' with 'if (count >= MAX_RECOVERY_VETOES && block.timestamp <= p1.lagEnds() && block.timestamp <= p2.lagEnds()) revert VetoesExhausted();' so that while the pair in force died by lag the freezer may veto without limit (the honest outcome is then an owner+guardian-agreed successor or the snapshot). Check the vault's 816-byte EIP-170 headroom (23,760 bytes at HEAD) and mirror into the twins.
priorArt: LG-4 (regression introduced by its fix), LG-I4, VLT-I1, design 6.9 Layer 3, BNB-I2

title: CometBFT and VeChain verifiers can be starved to permanent death by anyone's one-block updates
description: `update` is permissionless, must start from exactly the latest trusted header/table (CometBft L106 `u.trustedHash != latest` -> WrongAnchor; VeChain L108 `u.trustedId != latest`), and only requires the new head to be higher (CometBft L110 `u.height <= t.height`; VeChain L111 `_number(u.id) <= t.number`). Nothing requires the new head to be recent or to advance the clock meaningfully, while the verifier dies for good once `block.timestamp > latest.time + MAX_LAG` (CometBft L98, VeChain L100; slot proofs die with it, L155/L168, since every trusted header then is >1 day old). Scenario: (1) keeper K proves hops from the latest header L to a header near now; SP1 Groth16 proving takes minutes. (2) Attacker A, at least once per K's proving window (or by front-running K's tx in the public mempool), submits a valid proof of the real one-block hop L -> L+1 (Injective: next CometBFT height, +~0.65 s of chain time; VeChain: a block one slot after L in which A sent a 7-VTHO `VeChainStakerAttester.attest(table)` tx, +10 s), precomputed from public chain data. (3) latestHash/latestId moves, so K's proof reverts WrongAnchor; K must restart from L+1 and A repeats. Chain time of the latest header now advances by ~1 s (CometBFT) or 10 s (VeChain) per A-update while real time advances by the proving window, so after ~1 to 1.2 days `update` and `verifySlots` revert TooOld for everyone forever. Recovery only through the factory's 30-day ROTATION_DELAY (FAC-1), and the replacement is attackable the same way. Cost: ~1 update per proving window for ~1 day, e.g. 144-1440 x ~330k gas plus as many SP1 proofs of trivial hops (order of $100s-$1k). Impact while dead: no mint/claim/settlement on Injective/VeChain, an accepted rebalance fill with deliveries there cannot settle and its executor's bond is burned via failRebalance after deadline+GRACE unless the guardian cancels, and every evidence path against the chain (voidOrder, reportForgedDeposit, reportOutflow, slashRebalance) and recordExit is unavailable. Funds stay safe (burns need only Ethereum's proofs). Proven with a PoC against the real contracts and the repo's MockSP1Verifier (audit/poc/2026-10-04/A5-01__UpdateGrief.t.sol, both tests pass): ten-minute keeper attempts each preceded by a one-block attacker update -> every keeper update reverts WrongAnchor and the verifier reverts TooOld after ~1 day. The BNB, Tron, NEAR, Aptos and Sui verifiers are not affected: their minimal step is a whole epoch/period (real progress) or, for NEAR, an update within an epoch does not move the anchor. ARCHITECTURE.md 'Liveness' (L869-871) attributes a dead verifier only to keepers not advancing in time.
proposedFix: Require every update to land a recent head, so a third party's update can only keep the verifier alive. CometBftStateVerifier.sol: add `uint256 public constant MAX_UPDATE_AGE = 6 hours;` (and its getter in ICometBftStateVerifier) and after L113 `if (u.time > block.timestamp) revert InTheFuture(u.time);` add `if (block.timestamp > uint256(u.time) + MAX_UPDATE_AGE) revert TooOld(u.time);`. VeChainStateVerifier.sol: the same constant (VeChain's vouching needs ~70 blocks, ~12 min, plus proving, so 6 h is ample) and after L114 add `if (block.timestamp > uint256(u.time) + MAX_UPDATE_AGE) revert TooOld(u.time);`. Optionally also let an update start from any trusted header within MAX_LAG so in-flight keeper proofs survive: replace L94-L110 (CometBft) by `Trusted memory top = _trusted[latestHash]; ... Trusted memory t = _trusted[u.trustedHash]; if (t.height == 0 || u.trustedHeight != t.height || u.trustedTime != t.time) revert WrongAnchor(u.trustedHeight, u.trustedHash); if (block.timestamp > uint256(t.time) + MAX_LAG) revert TooOld(t.time); if (u.height <= top.height) revert BadPublicValues();` (VeChain analogously with `_number(u.id) <= top.number`). Regression test (name it per the review id): an attacker update to latest+1 dated `t+1` at `block.timestamp = t + 7 hours` reverts TooOld(t+1), and the PoC loop above no longer kills the verifier. Update the contracts' @dev text and ARCHITECTURE.md L869-871.
priorArt: none (TRN-6 is the Tron analogue of a front-run advance, but Tron's minimal step is a whole period; LG-2 fixed the same 'a block at a time' pattern for vault checkpoints)

title: BNB verifier needs each epoch block finalized by its direct child; one validator (or a missed attestation) stalls it for good
description: `advance` accepts epoch block E+1000 only with a quorum vote whose source is exactly E+1000 and target E+1001 (L96-97, `_checkVote` L240 `target = h.number + 1`, vote hash L253). Nothing can be skipped (spec 5.1), and once the latest set is >MAX_LAG old the verifier is dead (L91), replaced only by the 30-day rotation. Under bnb-chain/bsc v1.7.8 (the version the contract cites; checked in its source): votes on block N carry source = the justified block in N's snapshot (`vote_manager.go` UnderRules -> GetJustifiedNumberAndHash(N)), and a block becomes justified only through an attestation carried in a later header that targets it (`snapshot.go` updateAttestation); including an attestation is optional (`parlia.go` verifyVoteAttestation: `if attestation == nil { return nil }`), and since Fermi the producer may target any of 3 ancestors (`assembleVoteAttestation`, kAncestorGenerationDepth = 3). Hence the vote (E+1000 -> E+1001) exists only if header E+1001 carries an attestation targeting E+1000, and the keeper gets its aggregate only if a header among E+1002..E+1004 carries it (the fixture generator reads it from headers only, generate.py L203-214) or someone captured the p2p vote pool live. With turn length 8 (fixture: 21 validators, TL 8) and E a multiple of 1000, blocks E+1000..E+1007 belong to ONE validator's turn (`inturnValidator`: N / TL % n), so the producer of the epoch block alone can, consensus-validly, omit or retarget the attestation in E+1001 (or omit it in E+1002..E+1004): no honest vote (E+1000 -> E+1001) is then ever signed, `advance` can never record E+1000, and after 1 day the verifier stops for good. Any of ~21 validators can do this during its turn, which is far weaker than the 2/3 trust the verifier is meant to rest on; natural misses (votes for E+1000 not in the producer's pool 0.45 s later; BSC itself counts `notJustified`/`notContinuousJustified`, and Fermi's ancestor depth exists because parent attestations are missed) do the same at whatever their rate is, and the verifier must clear 192 epochs a day. Impact as for any dead verifier: BNB mints/claims/settlements stop for 30+ days, an accepted fill with BNB deliveries burns its executor's bond, and BNB evidence paths are unavailable; funds stay safe. Confidence medium only on how often it happens naturally; the single-validator path follows from the cited source.
priorArt: none (BNB-2 bounds staleness, not this liveness; spec 5.1 'Nothing can be skipped')

title: Checkpoint timestamp >= 2^63 wraps in the shared core's is_newer: a forged checkpoint starts the snapshot exit at once and locks the freezer out (Solana twin diverges from XindexVault)
description: `is_newer` checks `c.timestamp as i64 <= now` (checkpoint.rs:29). A u64 timestamp of 2^63 or more casts to a negative i64, so the 'not in the future' check passes for any such timestamp. `stall_start` (line 17) uses the same cast, so the stored checkpoint makes `stalled()` true at once, and `stall_start + SNAPSHOT_EXIT_DELAY` comes out negative. The Solana vault uses these functions directly: vault.rs:66-95 (`stall_start`, `stalled`, `check_newer`), recovery.rs:28-55 (`advance_checkpoint`) and recovery.rs:238-257 (`begin_snapshot`). The NEAR vault calls the same `checkpoint::is_newer` and `stall_start` (near/contracts/xindex-vault/src/lib.rs:613,896,1047). XindexVault.sol compares in uint256 (`c.timestamp > block.timestamp` reverts, line 759), so the EVM twin refuses such a checkpoint. Scenario. Precondition: P1 and P2 both accept a forged header leaf. This is the 'P1 and P2 both broken' threat model that VLT-2, VLT-4 and LG-3 defend against, and it is more correlated than it looks, since P1 and P2 run the same finality statement code. (1) Anyone calls `advance_checkpoint` with {block: last+1, timestamp: 1<<63, state_root: R_forged}. `check_newer` passes and the checkpoint is stored. `stalled()` is now true, so the function returns early. (2) In the same block, anyone calls `begin_snapshot`. `due` = i64::MIN + 187 days, so `now >= due` holds, and the snapshot becomes the forged checkpoint, for good. (3) From then on `freeze` and FREEZE messages are refused (payouts.rs:114, messages.rs:495, VLT-5). No successor can be proposed (`check_no_snapshot`), and no later checkpoint can replace the snapshot. (4) The attacker proves arbitrary storage under R_forged: `claim_snapshot` for fabricated holders and shares, and `deliver_recorded_burn` on fabricated `_sentMessages` marks. This drains every index's balance at 4% a day, or the floor. Honest holders cannot prove their real hub storage against a fabricated root, so they recover nothing. On the EVM twin the same forgery cannot force a snapshot sooner than 187 days, and during that time the freezer can hold payouts and the factory can respond. On Solana (and NEAR) the window is zero and the freezer is locked out at once. I ran the core's own functions to confirm: is_newer(forged)=true, stalled=true, snapshot due=-9223372036838619008 with now=1790000000 (audit/poc/2026-10-04/B1-01__wrap.rs).
proposedFix:
crates/xindex-core/src/checkpoint.rs. Never cast a u64 timestamp to i64 unchecked:
BEFORE (16-18):
  pub fn stall_start(timestamp: u64) -> i64 {
      timestamp as i64 + STALL_PERIOD
  }
AFTER:
  pub fn stall_start(timestamp: u64) -> i64 {
      i64::try_from(timestamp).unwrap_or(i64::MAX).saturating_add(STALL_PERIOD)
  }
BEFORE (26-31):
      c.block > last.block
          && c.timestamp > last.timestamp
          && c.timestamp as i64 <= now
          && c.state_root != [0u8; 32]
AFTER:
      c.block > last.block
          && c.timestamp > last.timestamp
          && i64::try_from(c.timestamp).is_ok_and(|t| t <= now)
          && c.state_root != [0u8; 32]
BEFORE (34-36): c.timestamp as i64 + STALL_PERIOD >= now
AFTER: i64::try_from(c.timestamp).is_ok_and(|t| t.saturating_add(STALL_PERIOD) >= now)
Also apply the twin rule to the Move vaults (sui/, aptos/) if they cast the same way. Regression test in solana/programs/xindex-vault/tests/recovery.rs, `test_b1_01_a_wrapped_timestamp_is_never_newer`: advance a checkpoint whose stub-proven timestamp is 1<<63. Expect VaultError::NotNewer, and expect `begin_snapshot` to still revert SnapshotNotDue. Add a core unit test that asserts `!is_newer(&last, &Checkpoint{block: last.block+1, timestamp: 1<<63, state_root: [1;32]}, now)`.
priorArt: none (relates to VLT-2/VLT-5/LG-2 threat model; SOL-7 built the recovery)

title: Nothing makes the vault program immutable before it holds coins: one upgrade-authority key controls all SOL until a manual --final
description: The EVM vault has no owner and cannot be upgraded by construction. The Solana vault is deployed through the upgradeable loader, and the program's header says it is protected only by a manual step: 'the deployer only initializes it, and on mainnet then removes the program's upgrade authority' (lib.rs:6-7; spec section 7 lines 800-801). No code enforces that step. `initialize` requires the upgrade authority to sign (setup.rs:41-44), which is right for front-running. But `register_index` (setup.rs:138-177), `deposit` (deposits.rs:45-106) and every delivery run whether or not the program is still upgradeable. Scenario: the deployer initializes, the factory registers the chain (`proposeChain` then `executeChain`), and indexes start taking SOL, while the upgrade authority is still a single hot key (the same key that signed `initialize`). Whoever holds that key, or anyone who compromises it, deploys a new program and transfers the treasury's whole balance out in one transaction. That bypasses P1/P2, the speed limit, the freezer and every delay. This breaks AGENTS.md's 'No admin power over funds... no upgrade' and the hot-key rule (the broadcasting key must hold no authority). The vault itself already enforces exactly this property for P1 and P2 (SOL-2, `check_immutable`), so the same check can be applied to the program itself. No Solana mainnet deployment procedure or script exists, and AGENTS.md's Deployment section lists none.
proposedFix:
solana/programs/xindex-vault/src/instructions/setup.rs. Refuse to register an index, and so any deposit or message, until the vault program itself is final. Devnet keeps its upgradeable build behind a feature.
In `RegisterIndex` add:
  #[account(constraint = program.programdata_address()? == Some(program_data.key()) @ VaultError::NotDeployer)]
  pub program: Program<'info, XindexVault>,
  pub program_data: Account<'info, ProgramData>,
In `handle_register_index`, before the predict_clone check:
  #[cfg(not(feature = "devnet"))]
  require!(ctx.accounts.program_data.upgrade_authority_address.is_none(), VaultError::VaultUpgradeable);
Add `VaultUpgradeable` to error.rs and `devnet = []` to Cargo.toml [features]. Test `test_b1_02_an_upgradeable_vault_registers_no_index` (built without `devnet`): it expects VaultUpgradeable while the authority is set, and success after `set-upgrade-authority --final`.
priorArt: SOL-2 (same property, for the verifiers only)

title: NEP-616 initial state is an arbitrary key/value map; nothing in the repo derives or verifies it against Vault::build, so seeded P1/P2 ranges or balances would be invisible
description: The NEAR vault is trusted to be keyless and immutable because its account `0s...` is the hash of (code hash, initial storage). But `DeterministicStateInit.data` is a raw BTreeMap<Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>> (sandbox.rs:251-262 builds it from `Vault::build` only inside a cfg(test) helper). Nothing on chain forces it to equal what `build` produces. A deployer can add any extra keys. The tests themselves show how: sandbox.rs:127-141 write a `ranges` entry as `[1] ++ verifier_id ++ headers_root -> (first,last)` with `patch_state`. Put the same entry in `state_init.data` for the P1 and P2 ids and `deliver`/`advance_checkpoint` accept a forged receipt/checkpoint under a made-up headers tree with no SNARK at all (light_client::verify_event only asks `ranges` for the root, lib.rs:1096-1110). Other seeds are just as possible: `indexes[x].balance/outflow`, `used`, `slots` (attest), a P1 `key` that is the attacker's own SP1 program, or `cap`/`outflow_floor`. The `config`, `verifier`, `range` and `index_state` views only show what is asked for by key, so a reviewer who inspects the account through views sees a normal vault. The only complete guard is: recompute the `0s` id from the intended config, `now` and code hash with `Vault::build`, and compare (or diff `view_state` against it). near/README.md only lists checks for the recovery proposer (lines 112-118); there is no deploy/verify binary in near/, and AGENTS.md says NEAR's vault 'goes up with its chain's own tools, as near/ says'. An EVM vault cannot carry seeded storage (its constructor is the only writer), so this is a new review burden the NEAR twin adds. Scenario: the owner (or whoever deploys) registers the account id via proposeChain; the 2-day listing window is the only review; a seeded vault accepts forged messages and pays out up to the 4%/day speed limit per index (the speed-limit buckets and floor are in the same raw state). Mitigations: factory listing delay, guardian cancel, mint cap, chain cap. Not exploited; process hazard.
proposedFix: near/README.md after line 118: add a mandatory step 3 'Verify the account before registering it': (a) run `cargo run -p xindex-vault-near --example initial_state -- <config.json> <now>` which prints the `0s` id and the borsh state map from `Vault::build` (move `initial_state` from tests/sandbox.rs:251-262 into `examples/initial_state.rs`, un-cfg(test)'d); (b) compare the id with the registered one and the Wasm hash with a reproducible build (`cargo near build reproducible-wasm`, pin the image and publish the expected hash); (c) `near view-state <id>` must equal the printed map key for key. Add `near/tools/verify_vault.sh` wrapping (a)-(c) and have `script/ConfigureChains.s.sol` docs require its output in the proposeChain announcement.
priorArt: none (SOL-1/SOL-2 concern Solana stub init and upgradeable verifiers; NEP-616 raw-state seeding not covered)

title: Anyone can kill P1 or P2 for good by landing stale one-epoch steps that void every honest in-flight proof
description:
`update` accepts a proof only from the exact stored anchor (`if (anchorIn != anchor) revert WrongAnchor`, FinalityVerifier.sol:91) and the statement accepts ANY finalized C1 with anchor.epoch < C1.epoch <= anchor.epoch + 225 (proofs/finality/src/statement.rs:171-179): nothing requires the new checkpoint to be recent. The lag clock (`lagEnds()`, :101-103, LG-4) is dated from the stored anchor's epoch, so a step to an old checkpoint moves the anchor (voiding every proof in flight from the previous anchor) while extending the clock by only 384 s per epoch stepped. A P1/P2 proof is a full proving job over the whole registry (36.6B prover gas on mainnet data; the prototype targets <=60 min end to end, so honest latency L is tens of minutes at best), while the attacker's next anchors are deterministic (anchor_out of step a->a+1 is fixed by the canonical chain), so it can prove the whole sequence a->a+1, a+1->a+2, ... in advance, in parallel, as soon as those epochs finalize.

Scenario (any vault chain, EVM or any twin): (1) stored anchor at epoch a; the honest relayer proves a->latest and broadcasts update. (2) The attacker front-runs it with its precomputed valid proof a->a+1; the honest update reverts WrongAnchor. (3) The honest relayer must re-prove from a+1 (time L) while the clock moved 384 s; the attacker front-runs again with a+1->a+2, and so on. Each round burns L of the day's slack for 6.4 min of extension. (4) When lagEnds() < now + L, no honest proof can land: at lagEnds()+1 every update reverts TooOld and the verifier is dead for good. Without mempool visibility the attacker simply lands a stale step every <L, which voids every honest proof just as well (about twice as many proofs). The honest relayer cannot pre-empt: the attacker picks among ~225 possible next anchors.

Confirmed with a PoC against the unmodified FinalityVerifier + MockSP1Verifier (audit/poc/2026-10-04/B5-01__StaleStepPoC.t.sol, `test_poc_staleOneEpochStepsKillTheVerifier`, PASS): with L = 47 min, 34 attacker proofs kill the verifier 27 h after the anchor's epoch; at the prototype's <= $50/proof target that is ~ $1,700.

Impact: with P1 or P2 dead the vault's `advanceCheckpoint` (both proofs, XindexVault.sol:586-601) and every loosening `deliver` (burns, settles, migrations, XindexVault.sol:225) stop; after STALL_PERIOD the vault refuses deposits; recovery needs the emergency multisig's successor plus a 30-day review with up to 2 vetoes, and the successor pair has the same flaw, so the attacker can repeat each cycle (about a day of service per ~37 days) and keep the vault out of both service and the 180-day snapshot exit. No coins are stolen. The same exact-anchor rule is in every twin: crates/xindex-core/src/light_client.rs:92-104 (`advance`, used by solana/programs/ethereum-verifier/src/lib.rs:329-366 and risc0-verifier, near/contracts/xindex-vault/src/lib.rs:478, stellar), and sui/sources/light_client.move:139 (aptos likewise). Not covered by LG-4 (which added the clock) or any earlier id.
priorArt: LG-4 (added the clock that this griefing exhausts); BNB-2 (same lag shape, but BNB proofs are cheap); none for the griefing itself

title: Stage A spec still specifies the pre-SA-07 settlement amounts (differences of floored backings)
description: The Stage A spec, which AGENTS.md names as 'the Stage A spec' and which section 3.2 presents as the settlement rule, still gives `out_i = floor(S*u_i/1e18) - floor(S*u'_i/1e18)` and `in_i = floor(S*u'_i/1e18) - floor(S*u_i/1e18)`. That is exactly the formula SA-07 (audit/2026-09-30-stage-a-red-team.md) found to pay an executor that delivers nothing, and the code no longer implements it: src/IndexHub.sol 449-455 (and its twin src/hybrid/HybridHubModule.sol 547-555) computes `out_i = floor(S*(u_i-u'_i)/1e18)` and `in_i = ceil(S*(u'_i-u_i)/1e18)`. ARCHITECTURE.md 3.3 was updated with SA-07; the spec was not, and neither was design/2026-09-29-v4-hybrid-architecture.md 407-409 ('Amounts are differences of floored backing, as in v3'). Concrete divergence (exact integers): S = 0.5e18 shares, a shrinking leg u=2 -> u'=1 and a growing leg u=2 -> u'=3. Spec: out = floor(1) - floor(0.5) = 1, in = floor(1.5) - floor(1) = 0, so an empty executor is paid one raw unit. Code: out = floor(0.5) = 0, in = ceil(0.5) = 1. Impact: no on-chain impact today; a future change made 'to spec' (or an external auditor or re-implementation, e.g. a new vault-chain twin, that follows the spec) reintroduces SA-07. The spec also still claims the invariant follows from differences of floors, so its reasoning no longer matches the code's.
proposedFix: design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-a-spec.md lines 115-117, before: "sold: `out_i = ⌊S·u_i/1e18⌋ − ⌊S·u'_i/1e18⌋`; one above is bought: `in_i = ⌊S·u'_i/1e18⌋ − ⌊S·u_i/1e18⌋`." After: "sold: `out_i = ⌊S·(u_i − u'_i)/1e18⌋`; one above is bought: `in_i = ⌈S·(u'_i − u_i)/1e18⌉`. Each leg's change in backing is rounded the holders' way on its own (SA-07); the invariant survives since ⌊a − b⌋ ≤ ⌊a⌋ − ⌊b⌋ and ⌊a + b⌋ ≤ ⌊a⌋ + ⌈b⌉." And design/2026-09-29-v4-hybrid-architecture.md line 408-409, before: "Amounts are differences of floored backing, as in v3, so they come only from supply and units." After: "Amounts are each leg's change in backing, rounded down when it leaves and up when it comes back (SA-07), so they come only from supply and units."
priorArt: SA-07 (fix applied to code and ARCHITECTURE.md, not to the spec or the design document)

title: An accepted fill can become unsettleable through no fault of its executor, and anyone then burns the bond
description: Once a fill is accepted its legs, recipients and λ are fixed, and the only ways out are settleRebalance, failRebalance (bond burned) and the guardian's cancelRebalance (bond returned). settleRebalance pays each sold Ethereum leg with IERC20(token).safeTransfer(f.executor, out[i]) (lines 329-331), so a sold component that is paused during the window (WBTC is pausable; AGENTS.md lists it as a component to label) makes every settlement revert. The same happens when the vault of a bought leg is frozen before the deliveries land (XindexVault.deposit refuses while frozen or stalled): a factory freezeChain by the owner/guardian, or reportOutflow evidence from any index (payouts=true), freezes the vault, and _checkMovingChains is only checked at acceptance. Scenario: (1) executor E accepts a fill selling WBTC, posting a bond of 0.1% of supply and the Ethereum deliveries; (2) WBTC's admin pauses transfers (or the chain's vault is frozen); (3) settleRebalance reverts at the WBTC transfer (or the deliveries cannot be deposited); (4) at deadline + SETTLE_GRACE (12h after acceptance) any stranger calls failRebalance -> _unwind(true) burns E's bond (lines 394-402, 418). While the fill sits Accepted, claimOrder and acceptMigration revert RebalanceInProgress. Only the guardian, acting within those 12 hours, can return the bond. Stage A's atomic fill simply reverts with no bond at stake, and the hub's own pattern elsewhere is 'claims, never transfers, so a paused token cannot block' (_fail, _unwind, MOD-4's zero-recipient vault legs). The spec's justification for the burn ('the executor pays for an abandoned fill') assumes the abandonment is the executor's. Impact: an innocent executor loses 0.1% of the index's supply in shares; executors will price this risk or avoid fills selling pausable components. Mitigations: pauses/freezes inside a 12h window are rare; the guardian can cancel.
priorArt: none (related: MOD-4 zero-recipient vault legs, MOD-I5 settle ignores freezes, DA-14/RT-01 keep mask)

title: A fill on an index with no supply is free (no bond, no deliveries, no proofs), so anyone can stall or break the creator's locked seed
description: Only the creator may seed an empty index (HUB-2), and the seed order is Locked for 24h with totalSupply still 0. If an auction is live then (anyone may start one MIN_REBALANCE_INTERVAL after creation once supplies have moved >= MIN_BAND), a stranger can call acceptRebalance(recipients, []): supply = 0 so bond = mulDiv(0, ..) = 0 (line 232), every amountsIn is 0, and _moveShares(msg.sender, this, 0) succeeds with no shares held (line 260). settleRebalance with m empty ChainProofs then succeeds too: _fillSettlement(0) gives out = need = 0, so _proveDeliveries returns early and _checkLeg is skipped; the units become ceil(lambdaMax*u/r) (nothing sells, so lambda = lambdaMax). test_aFillSendingNothingIsTakenAtLambdaMax shows exactly this (bond 0, _oneEmpty() proofs). Consequences: (a) at claim, HybridHub._covered (HybridHub.sol 240, 265-274) compares the seed's amounts at the old units with the new ones; every component whose ratio was below lambdaMax gained >= MIN_BAND, so the seed fails (escrow to claims, INTAKE_FAILED) and the creator must redo the order, the deposits on every chain and the 24h lock; or (b) the stranger just leaves the free fill Accepted, and claimOrder reverts RebalanceInProgress (HybridHub.sol 224) until someone calls failRebalance after deadline + GRACE (12h), which burns a zero bond. Cost to the griefer: gas. Stage A's empty-index settlement at lambdaMax (R14, XA-27) is harmless because issue is atomic; the hybrid's lock turns it into a lever. Impact: delay and repeated proving costs for the creator; no funds lost.

title: The mint cap is a first-come allowance: a capitalised actor can hold it full and have every other order failed
description: MINT_LIMIT is one per-index allowance of 4% of supply over 25 hourly buckets, consumed at settleOrder (HybridHub.sol 182) by whoever settles first, with no share per minter. Shares of an order that later fails at claim or is voided keep their room. An actor with about 4% of the index's value in its components can, each time buckets age out, open an order for mintRoom() shares, deposit, and settle it, then claim after the lock and redeem or sell. Every other minter's settleOrder then reverts MintCapExceeded; once their deadline + SETTLE_GRACE passes, anyone (the same actor) calls failOrder (HybridHub.sol 277-282) and their orders fail, to be redone at the cost of fresh deposits and state proofs on every chain. The actor's redemptions also draw the vault's 4% speed limit, whose release() is first-come too, so honest redeemers' vault legs can queue behind them. Cost: capital tied up roughly a day or two per cycle plus gas and proofs, no loss of principal. Impact: primary issuance on that index is denied for as long as the actor pays; holders can still redeem and trade. README's Stage B limitations describe the cap as a rate, not as a contested resource, and no earlier review covers its monopolisation.
proposedFix:
Document it, README.md after line 543 (Stage B limitations):
+- **The mint cap is first come, first served.** Anyone settling an order uses the index's 4% a day; a holder of enough of the components can keep it full, and orders that cannot settle are failed by anyone SETTLE_GRACE after their deadline, their deposits refunded. Mints then wait until the cap frees; holders redeem and trade throughout.
Optionally soften the forced failure: in HybridHub.failOrder (lines 277-282) let strangers fail an order only once its deadline + SETTLE_GRACE has passed AND the order would fit the current mintRoom(), or lengthen SETTLE_GRACE for orders the cap refused.
priorArt: none (HUB-2 and MOD-2 concern the cap's bound, not its allocation)

title: The hub never refuses a vault state older than one it already accepted, which the verifier interface and spec 5.1 require of it
description: IVaultStateVerifier.verifySlots (src/interfaces/IVaultStateVerifier.sol 9-11) says: 'A caller comparing it with a deadline must also refuse a state older than one it already accepted', and spec 5.1 (lines 226-227) says 'The hub must also refuse a state older than one it has already accepted from the same vault', as the complement of the BNB verifier's MAX_LAG and MAX_SPAN: a superseded validator set, possibly past BNB's slashing window, can still sign blocks of its own window up to a day back. _provenSlot only checks time > notBefore (line 273) and keeps no high-water mark, so settleOrder, voidOrder, reconfirmOrder, slashRebalance and reportForgedDeposit each accept any state after their lower bound, including one older than a state the hub already used. A forgery therefore needs 2/3 of any BNB set (or 19 of any Tron list) from the last day, not of the current one. Impact is bounded: a forged settle is still voidable during the lock by an honest proof, and a forged void or slash freezes one chain's mints for 14 days, which an attacker could repeat from a fresh index of its own; a per-index mark would not stop that, so the stated rule is weaker than the docs imply as well as unimplemented. Either the rule is intended and missing, or the interface and the spec overstate what the hub does.
proposedFix:
Pick one. (a) Correct the documents to what the hub relies on: src/interfaces/IVaultStateVerifier.sol lines 9-10:
-    /// @return timestamp The block's timestamp, in seconds. A caller comparing it with a deadline must also refuse a
-    ///         state older than one it already accepted.
+    /// @return timestamp The block's timestamp, in seconds. A caller bounds it below by its own deadline or freeze; the
+    ///         verifier bounds its age by MAX_LAG.
and design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-b-spec.md line 226-227: drop 'The hub must also refuse a state older than one it has already accepted from the same vault.' and state that every hub read is bounded below by a deadline or freeze. (b) Or enforce a per-chain high-water mark where it binds every index: a factory function the hub calls from _provenSlot, e.g. `IHybridIndexFactory.noteState(chainId, time)` that reverts when time < lastState[chainId] and records the maximum, made non-view along the settle/void/slash paths (the module and extension are near 24KB, so this costs size).
priorArt: BNB-2 (MAX_LAG/MAX_SPAN on the verifier side), BNB-I1

title: VLT-4 fix incomplete: a newer cap cut relayed on one proof leaves the nonce mark, so an older raise delivered afterwards queues and undoes it
description:
VLT-4 ("an older cap raise delivered late undid a newer cut") was fixed by refusing a governance message whose nonce is not above `governanceNonce[key]`, a mark that only a message on both proofs moves (L295-297).

A cut loosens nothing (`_needsBoth` is false, L400-404). So it may be relayed on one proof, and without waiting for the checkpoint. It then applies at once (L303-305) without moving the mark. Its id is marked `used` (L231-232), so the same message can never be delivered again on both proofs to move the mark.

Scenario, with honest actors only:
1. The owner proposes and executes a raise R (nonce n), then a cut C for the same token (nonce n+1).
2. A relayer delivers C first. This is the natural order, since a cut needs no checkpoint, and one proof is cheaper.
3. Anyone delivers R on both proofs once the checkpoint covers it. Its nonce n is above the unmoved mark, so it is queued as loosening (L299-302).
4. Seven days later anyone calls `applyChange`, and R's cap and floor replace C's.

The raised floor lifts the speed limit for small balances, and the raised cap reopens deposits. Only the freezer's `cancelChange`, or a fresh cut by the owner, stops it.

PoC, run green in a scratch copy, on test/XindexVault.t.sol's VaultTestBase:
```
bytes memory olderRaise = _payload(CAP_UPDATE, factory, abi.encode(bytes32(0), CAP*2, FLOOR*10));
bytes memory newerCut  = _payload(CAP_UPDATE, factory, abi.encode(bytes32(0), CAP/2, FLOOR));
vault.deliver(_proof(factory, newerCut), "");          // one proof: applied, mark unmoved
uint256 readyAt = block.timestamp + vault.GOVERNANCE_DELAY();
_deliver(factory, olderRaise);                          // both proofs: queued
vm.warp(readyAt);
vault.applyChange(CAP_UPDATE, abi.encode(bytes32(0), CAP*2, FLOOR*10), readyAt);
assertEq(vault.cap(address(0)), CAP*2);                 // the older raise undid the newer cut
```
The existing tests (`test_VLT4_...`, `test_FAC2_VLT4_...`) deliver the newer cut on both proofs only. The twins share the rule: Solana messages.rs:466-477, Sui vault.move:1133, Aptos vault.move:1297.

title: A FREEZE message never expires: one delivered late freezes the vault for 14 days from its delivery, at a stranger's chosen time
description:
The factory's FREEZE carries an empty body (HybridIndexFactory.sol:132). The vault applies it with no nonce check (L289-292), on one proof, with no checkpoint requirement. It freezes until `block.timestamp + FREEZE_DURATION` at delivery (L571-575), not until the Ethereum-side freeze ends (`_freezes[chainId].until`, HybridIndexFactory.sol:129-130). Each FREEZE runs once (`used[id]`), but one that was never delivered stays deliverable until a snapshot. `resendMessage` (L154-158) also lets anyone re-emit it in a fresh block that newly rotated verifiers cover.

Scenario:
1. The guardian calls `freezeChain(X)` at T. Nobody delivers the FREEZE: the vault's freezer had already frozen the vault directly, or the freeze was meant for mints.
2. The factory's freeze ends at T+14d.
3. Months later a stranger delivers the old FREEZE and the vault freezes for another 14 days. Payouts, refunds and deposits stop, and so does every waiting `applyChange`, such as a VERIFIER_ROTATION scheduled ahead of an Ethereum fork.

Each undelivered FREEZE is a 14-day pause that anyone can fire at a time of their choosing. It needs no broken proof system: the message is genuine.

PoC, run green in a scratch copy: `bytes memory freeze = _payload(FREEZE, factory, ""); vm.warp(block.timestamp + 300 days); _fresh(); vault.deliver(_proof(factory, freeze), ""); assertEq(vault.frozenUntil(), block.timestamp + 14 days);`. The Solana twin does the same: `freeze_until(config, now, ..)`, messages.rs:490-495.
priorArt: VLT-5 (no freeze after the snapshot), BNB-I2; none on late delivery

title: The factory accepts vault token ids wider than 160 bits, and the hub silently truncates them, so two listings can share one deposit
description:
`proposeVaultListing(chainId, tokenId, supply)` takes any `bytes32` tokenId.

Every vault represents a token in 20 bytes. Intake and index digests carry `address[] tokens` (HybridHubStorage.sol:309-321), and the EVM vault refuses wider ids (`_toAddress`, XindexVault.sol:837-840). The hub maps a component to its vault token with `_vaultAddress(_vaultTokenOf[i])`, a silent truncation (HybridHubStorage.sol:219-221, used by `_totalOf` at L330).

Scenario, through an owner error that a public 2-day delay does not flag:
1. The owner lists a coin on chain X under tokenId `bytes32(uint256(1) << 160)` beside the native coin's tokenId 0, and an index holds both.
2. `settleOrder` credits the same native intake total to both components (`_settleChain`, HybridHub.sol:209-215).
3. One deposit of max(required) satisfies both, and `claimOrder` adds it to both books (L252). The book overstates the vault.
4. Every BURN of the second component reverts `NotAnAddress` on the EVM vault, so that leg is never paid.

The NatSpec of `_vaultAddress` ("Stage B's vaults all run on EVM chains") is stale too: Solana, NEAR, Stellar, Sui and Aptos vaults are 32-byte ids.
proposedFix:
Fail closed at listing. In src/HybridIndexFactory.sol:102-104, add:
```
         if (_chains[chainId].vault == bytes32(0)) revert UnknownChain(chainId);
+        // Every vault's digests carry a token as 20 bytes (`address[]`), and the hub compares it so.
+        if (uint256(tokenId) >> 160 != 0) revert InvalidTokenId(tokenId);
```
Declare `error InvalidTokenId(bytes32 tokenId);` in IHybridIndexFactory. Optionally make `_vaultAddress` revert on high bits instead of truncating (HybridHubStorage.sol:219-221), and fix its NatSpec to "a vault's or a vault token's 32-byte id, of which every vault's digests and state verifiers use the low 20 bytes". Test: `proposeVaultListing(chainId, bytes32(uint256(1) << 160), 1e18)` reverts `InvalidTokenId`.

title: No honest successor can pass the continuity test: a FinalityVerifier pair cannot prove a checkpoint older than a day, so every stall ends in owner-supplied custom code or the 187-day snapshot
description: proposeSuccessor requires (a) the new pair to return exactly the vault's _checkpoint from verifyCheckpoint (623-624) and (c) to verifyEvent the last both-proof message (628-633). On FinalityVerifier, the only Ethereum-event verifier in the repository, both succeed only for a block inside a range recorded by update (_checkHeader 166-168: UnknownHeaders / NotInRange), and the constructor (76-81) records none. A stalled vault's checkpoint is by definition more than STALL_PERIOD (7 days) old, so a new FinalityVerifier can cover it only from an anchor at or before that block, i.e. more than 7 days old, and update refuses any proof once a day has passed since the anchor's epoch began (87, LG-4). A FinalityVerifier pair can therefore pass (a) only if it was deployed and kept updated since before the vault's last checkpoint: impossible after an unannounced format break (nobody had a prover for the new rules then) and pointless after a lag death (the same proofs would have kept the old pair alive). So the documented recovery cannot be performed with the repository's code: spec 10 lines 1072 ('a verifier stops for good and is rotated') and 1113-1115 / LG-I4 ('the vault stalls, and a successor pair replaces it by stall recovery'), README 551-553 ('stops for good and must be replaced') and IEthereumEventVerifier.verifyCheckpoint's NatSpec all describe a successor that proves descent, which nothing implements. The real outcomes of any stall are either custom verifier code from the owner's emergency multisig, which holders must trust because the continuity test is that code's own answer (VLT-I1), or every coin on the chain waiting 187 days for the snapshot exit with no burn paid meanwhile (NotCheckpointed, 228-230). Honest scenario, no attacker: either proving service (SP1's network, Bonsai or the operator's GPUs; latency never measured) is down for ~24h; P1 or P2 dies; every vault it serves stalls a week later and locks all holders' coins on that chain for up to 187 days, unless they accept owner-written verifiers. README 546-553 presents a P1/P2 death beside the state verifiers', whose death leaves burns paying (549); a P1/P2 death stops burns too, and that is not stated. Spec 5.6 says only that a successor's proof of descent 'is not built', not that LG-4 makes the existing verifier unusable as a successor.
proposedFix: Make an honest successor constructible: let a FinalityVerifier inherit proven ranges from its predecessor, so it proves (a) and (c) from data already proven and only (b) rests on its fresh anchor, which the 30-day review checks as any first anchor is checked. src/verifiers/FinalityVerifier.sol 76-81, before: 'constructor(bytes32 initialAnchor, uint64 initialEpoch, uint256 genesisTime) {' ... after: 'constructor(bytes32 initialAnchor, uint64 initialEpoch, uint256 genesisTime, FinalityVerifier predecessor, bytes32[] memory inherited) {' plus, after the existing assignments, 'for (uint256 i = 0; i < inherited.length; ++i) { Range memory r = predecessor.range(inherited[i]); if (r.last == 0) revert UnknownHeaders(inherited[i]); _ranges[inherited[i]] = r; }' (EthereumFinalityVerifier/RiscZeroFinalityVerifier and DeployVault pass address(0)/[] for a first deployment; skip the loop when predecessor is zero), with a test that a successor pair inheriting the dead pair's last ranges passes proposeSuccessor (a), (b) and (c) and is adopted. If not built, correct the documents instead: spec 1072 'and is rotated' -> 'and every payout on its vaults waits for a successor the owner's emergency multisig supplies, whose code holders must trust, or for the snapshot exit 187 days later'; the same at spec 1113-1115, README 551-553 (and say burns stop too) and AGENTS.md 430-438.
priorArt: LG-4, LG-I4, VLT-I1, spec 5.6 'Not built: A successor's proof of descent'

title: The stall is keyed to checkpoints only: a break of receipt proofs alone leaves the vault unable to deliver anything yet never stalled, so recovery and the snapshot exit never open
description: stalled() (604-606) depends only on the last checkpoint's age, and advanceCheckpoint (586-601) needs only verifyCheckpoint, i.e. a header leaf in a range the zk statement recorded. Delivering anything needs verifyEvent, i.e. a Merkle-Patricia receipt proof against that header's receiptsRoot (FinalityVerifier 114-153). An Ethereum change that breaks receipt proofs but not the finality statement or the RLP header chain (for example SSZ receipts, EIP-6466, which changes what receiptsRoot commits to while headers stay RLP) leaves P1/P2 updating and checkpoints advancing, while no BURN, settle, refund or VERIFIER_ROTATION can ever be delivered. The vault is then never stalled, so proposeSuccessor (619) and beginSnapshot (676-677) never open, and the factory cannot rotate the pair because the rotation is itself undeliverable. Honest keepers on the README's schedule (838) keep it that way automatically; once they stop, any party willing to pay for one SP1 and one RISC Zero proof a day plus an advanceCheckpoint a week can hold every holder's coins on that chain indefinitely. Design 6.9 promises that coins are never stuck for good and Layer 2 that an unknown fork 'can stop payouts'; here it stops them with no path out. Conditional on such a fork arriving without a timely rotation (the owner or guardian missing the 90-day lead), hence LOW.
proposedFix: Make a checkpoint count only if the pair can still prove a receipt in it: give the factory a permissionless 'function heartbeat() external { emit Heartbeat(block.number); }', and have advanceCheckpoint take two more proofs, 'function advanceCheckpoint(bytes calldata proof1, bytes calldata proof2, bytes calldata event1, bytes calldata event2)', adding after _checkNewer(c) (589): '(uint256 b1, address e1,,,) = p1.verifyEvent(event1); (uint256 b2, address e2,,,) = p2.verifyEvent(event2); if (e1 != FACTORY || e2 != FACTORY || b1 != b2 || b1 > c.blockNumber || b1 + HEARTBEAT_WINDOW < c.blockNumber) revert NotNewer(c.blockNumber, c.timestamp);' so a pair that no longer proves receipts cannot keep the vault out of a stall (and adoptSuccessor likewise). Mind the 816-byte EIP-170 headroom and the twins; alternatively document the gap and the operational response (all keepers stop advancing) in spec 5.6 and the README known limitations.

title: paidTotal NatSpec and ARCHITECTURE.md say it can never exceed what the index sent, but snapshot claims add to it
description: IXindexVault.paidTotal: 'It can never exceed what the index sent out in BURN and MIGRATE messages.' ARCHITECTURE.md 765: '`paidTotal` counts every payout, which can never exceed what the index sent.' claimSnapshot (XindexVault 689-716) books an Owed and pays it through _release, which adds every payment to paidTotal (450), although the index never sent it. So after a snapshot exit paidTotal exceeds the index's sentOut by design, which is exactly why VLT-I6 made reportOutflow refuse an exited chain. A watcher or integrator that takes the documented invariant at its word (paidTotal > sentOut means both Ethereum proofs broke) raises a false alarm on every exited vault.
priorArt: VLT-I6 (fixed the hub side, not these docs)

title: NEAR verifier moves to epoch E+1 on any block of E, after which no head of E can be recorded: NEAR proofs can be held about one epoch (~7 h) behind, past the hub's 6-hour GRACE
description:
Each NEAR block in epoch E carries next_bp_hash, which commits to E+1's producers. nearcore's create_light_client_block always fills next_bps, mid-epoch heads included. The statement (proofs/near/statement/src/lib.rs:224-233) moves `epoch` to next_epoch_id on the first block that has next_bps, and the head may be that very block. NearStateVerifier.update (lines 121-131) then stores epochId = E+1 and namedAt = that block's time. It holds only one (epochId, producersHash), and every block of a later proof must have epoch_id == the stored epoch (lib.rs:213). So once the verifier sits at E+1, no block of E can be recorded as a head for the rest of E, and a vault attest that runs after the last recorded head stays unprovable (`_proveOutcome` line 186 needs a recorded head) until a block of E+1 is recorded.

The repo's own reference flow does this. In proofs/near/fixtures/mainnet.json, the head (block 218394743, epoch 0x4098e5..) carries next_bps, and public_values' epochOut is 0x6ff7fa.., its next_epoch_id. test_update_followsMainnet (test/NearStateVerifier.t.sol:183-215) asserts that the verifier moves to E+1. That head is 4,812 blocks (2,821 s) after E-1's last final block. With 43,200-block epochs at the fixture's own 0.586 s per block, an epoch lasts about 7.0 h, so about 38,400 blocks (about 6.25 h) of E are left that no proof can record.

Griefing scenario (permissionless, one SP1 proof and about 0.3M gas per epoch):
1. When the chain enters epoch E and the verifier is at E, the griefer calls update with blocks=[the first final block of E, with next_bps]. The verifier moves to E+1 with a head at the start of E.
2. For the rest of E, no keeper can record a head (refused with WrongAnchor, or WrongEpoch in the statement).
3. When E+1 starts, the griefer repeats the call with the first final block of E+1, and so on every epoch.
Heads then exist only near each epoch's start, so an attest made at time t becomes provable only at the next epoch start, up to about 7.0 h later, plus proving time.

Impact on the hub:
- (a) settleOrder needs every chain's intake proven at a time after the order's deadline (HybridHub.sol:207, notBefore = deadline). failOrder is open to anyone at deadline + GRACE, 6 h (HybridHub.sol:277-281; GRACE in HybridHubStorage.sol:26). Under the grief, every order of an index holding a NEAR vault coin whose deadline falls in roughly the first 1 h plus proving latency of a NEAR epoch (about 15-25% of orders) cannot be settled before a griefer fails it. Its escrow and deposits are refunded, so this is mint DoS, not theft.
- (b) A rebalance fill gets DELIVERY_WINDOW + GRACE = 12 h from acceptance (HybridHubModule.sol:46, 234, 397-399). An executor who delivers to the NEAR vault in roughly the last 5 h of the window may get no provable head before acceptance + 12 h, and anyone then calls failRebalance, which burns its bond (0.1% of supply in shares).
- The verifier cannot be bricked this way, because each transition still leaves 24 h minus one epoch. The damage is the freshness of proofs.

Root cause: nearcore's light client (validate_and_update_head) keeps producers for both head.epoch_id and head.next_epoch_id and changes its epoch only when it accepts a block of the next epoch. The statement changes epoch as soon as a block names the next producers. Prior audits do not cover NearStateVerifier.
priorArt: none (no prior audit covers NearStateVerifier or proofs/near)

title: StellarStateVerifier's 1-day MAX_LAG does not bound retired or leaked keys, as its NatSpec claims: the signers write the close time, and the pinned quorum set never expires
description:
The comment at lines 79-80 and the interface's MAX_LAG NatSpec say that keys retired or leaked later could sign a ledger dated long ago, and that a day bounds that, 'as it does for every other verifier'. That is not so. The close time checked (v.closeTime) is header N's scp_value.close_time (proofs/stellar/statement/src/lib.rs:380-385). Header N is fixed only through headers N..M-1, the transaction set and the StellarValue, all of which the same EXTERNALIZE signers commit to. A coalition holding a threshold of the pinned keys (for Tier 1, 2 of 3 validators in 7 of 10 organisations) can therefore sign EXTERNALIZE for a fabricated slot whose headers carry close time = now, and a result set holding a vault `attest` event with any slots and values. verifySlots accepts it, and the hub would accept forged intake digests.

The other verifiers measure their lag from when Ethereum learned the set (named time, epoch start, anchor), so a superseded set expires within a day. Stellar's QUORUM_SET_HASH is immutable and trusted for the verifier's whole registered life. After any Tier 1 key rotation or departure, the retired keys stay trusted until a replacement passes the factory's 30-day ROTATION_DELAY (FAC-1). The spec says 'Tier 1's changes have no on-chain anchor' (stage B spec, section 8 table), but the code tells reviewers the exposure is bounded to a day, and it is not.
priorArt: FAC-1 (ROTATION_DELAY); stage B spec section 8 notes Tier 1 has no on-chain anchor

title: Pinned Groth16 verifier checks are self-declared identity: a proxy or any contract that answers two view calls passes
description: ScriptUtils.isSp1Verifier (used by DeployStateVerifier for NEAR, Stellar, Injective, VeChain and Aptos, lines 309/339/417/446/477) and DeployVault.checkVerifiers (script/DeployVault.s.sol 190-202) accept a verifier if it answers VERIFIER_HASH()/VERSION() (SP1) or SELECTOR()/VERSION() (RISC Zero) with the pinned values. That is a name, not code. NatSpec says 'An owned gateway answers neither, so it is refused too', README.md:678-680 says the script 'refuses any Groth16 verifier but SP1's v6.0.0 ... and RISC Zero's 3.0.0 ... so an owned gateway, router or emergency stop is refused', and AGENTS.md ('Scripts') says DeployVault refuses 'any Groth16 verifier but the pinned SP1 and RISC Zero ones'. An OWNED proxy (OZ TransparentUpgradeableProxy/ERC1967 whose implementation is the real or a mock verifier) forwards the identity views and passes. I confirmed this in a scratch copy: a TransparentUpgradeableProxy (admin = attacker) over MockSP1Verifier and one over MockRiscZeroVerifier pass DeployVault.checkVerifiers without revert. Scenario: the broadcasting key (or an operator pasting a wrong address) supplies VAULT_SP1_VERIFIER and VAULT_RISC_ZERO_VERIFIER as two such proxies; check() passes; XindexVault stores them as P1/P2 immutables; the proxy admin later upgrades both to accept any proof, after which any message can be 'proven' and the vault drained at the speed limit (4%/day) until the freezer acts. This violates the hot-key rule (the broadcaster ends up holding authority over every payout) and the documented guarantee. Mitigations: the owner Safe/guardian review the chain registration (LISTING_DELAY 2 days), the speed limit, and both P1 and P2 must be forged. tron/README.md:118-120 and tron/deploy-test.mjs admit 'a name is no proof of code', but only for TRON, where the script can deploy the vendored verifiers itself; the EVM path (DeployVault) and every DeployStateVerifier chain have no such option and no codehash pin, and the repository's own mocks pass the check by design.
proposedFix: Pin runtime code, not names. script/ScriptUtils.sol: add `bytes32 internal constant SP1_VERIFIER_CODEHASH = 0x<codehash of the official SP1VerifierGroth16 v6.0.0>;` (no immutables, so one hash) and `RISC_ZERO_VERIFIER_CODEHASH` (3.0.0 with its published control ids), each read from the official deployments by a fork test like UNIVERSAL_ROUTER_CODEHASH in test/fork/MainnetAddresses.fork.t.sol. Then: `function isSp1Verifier(address v) internal view returns (bool) { return v.codehash == SP1_VERIFIER_CODEHASH && answers(v, abi.encodeCall(ISP1Groth16Identity.VERIFIER_HASH, ()), abi.encode(SP1_VERIFIER_HASH)) && answers(v, ...VERSION...); }` and the same codehash test in DeployVault.checkVerifiers (lines 192-201). In tron/deploy.mjs (checkSp1/checkRiscZero 185-201) and vechain/deploy.mjs (204-218) compare keccak256(chain code) with the codehash of the locally built vendored verifier (build output) or the pinned official one. Where a chain has no official deployment, keep the 'deploy the vendored verifier yourself' path and make it the only accepted one. Add to test/Scripts.t.sol: `test_A7_aProxyOverThePinnedVerifierIsRefused` that wraps MockSP1Verifier/MockRiscZeroVerifier in a TransparentUpgradeableProxy and expects DeployVault.WrongVerifier. (The mocks then need their codehash allowed in tests via vm.etch of the official runtime code, or a script-level override used only by tests.)

title: State-verifier review helpers read only the anchor: no code or trust-bearing immutable is checked for six verifiers, and NEAR and Stellar have no review helper
description: README.md:742-748 says that during the chain's listing delay 'the owner and guardian review' the verifier: checkBnb/checkTron confirm the code and the anchor, and 'checkSui, checkInjective, checkVeChain and checkAptos confirm the four newer verifiers hold their anchor files' anchors; their code cannot be compared by hash, since their immutables are in it'. The helpers (checkAptos 493-497, checkSui 503-508, checkInjective 513-517, checkVeChain 522-526) read only the latest trusted epoch/header/table and its time. None reads SP1_VERIFIER, PROGRAM_KEY, CHAIN_ID, VAULT/VAULT_ID/PACKAGE/ATTESTER or COSMOS_CHAIN_ID_HASH, all public immutables (src/verifiers/CometBftStateVerifier.sol 40-48, VeChainStateVerifier.sol 45-53, AptosStateVerifier.sol 46-54, SuiStateVerifier.sol 70-74), and none can detect different code. NEAR (deployNear 298-321) and Stellar (deployStellar 327-346) have no helper at all (README:745-747 leaves those to manual reads). A verifier is the trust root for every index's mints on that chain, and ConfigureChains.proposeChain/HybridIndexFactory.proposeChain only require `verifier.code.length != 0`. Scenario: a verifier built from other source (accepts any proof), or from this source with an attacker's SP1 verifier or program key, but with the real anchor, passes checkInjective/checkVeChain/checkAptos/checkSui; a reviewer who relies on the helper approves the 2-day proposal. The deploy-time checks (isSp1Verifier etc.) run only when the script itself deploys, so a verifier deployed by anyone else is never checked. Mitigations: human review of verified source, guardian veto, 4%/day mint cap, evidence freezes.
proposedFix: Make every check* compare the trust-bearing values and the code, and add checkNear/checkStellar. Code can be compared despite immutables by building a reference with the same arguments and comparing runtime hashes (the helper then becomes non-view, which is fine under `forge script`). Example for Injective (script/DeployStateVerifier.s.sol 513-517): `function checkInjective(address verifier, ISP1Verifier sp1, bytes32 programKey, uint256 chainId, string memory cosmos, address vault, uint64 height, bytes32 hash, uint64 time) public { CometBftStateVerifier v = CometBftStateVerifier(verifier); if (address(v.SP1_VERIFIER()) != address(sp1) || v.PROGRAM_KEY() != programKey || v.CHAIN_ID() != chainId || v.VAULT() != vault || v.COSMOS_CHAIN_ID_HASH() != keccak256(bytes(cosmos))) revert WrongAnchor(verifier); CometBftStateVerifier ref = new CometBftStateVerifier(sp1, programKey, chainId, cosmos, vault, height, hash, time); if (verifier.codehash != address(ref).codehash) revert WrongCode(verifier); ITrusted...; }` and likewise for Sui, VeChain, Aptos, Near, Stellar; and call it from each deploy function so the deploy log and the review share one code path. Update README:742-748 and add tests that a verifier built with another programKey/sp1/vault is refused (WrongAnchor) and one with different code is refused (WrongCode).

title: ConfigureChains has no RT-06/XA-11 protection: a guardian's cancelled chain proposal, cancelled first listing or delisting is proposed again by the next routine run
description: ConfigureWhitelist deliberately never proposes a first listing unless LIST names the token and never relists unless RELIST names it, because nothing on chain records a guardian cancel/delist (RT-06, XA-11; audit/2026-09-24-red-team.md RT-06). ConfigureChains, written later, has no equivalent. shouldProposeChain (133-170) returns true for any entry whose chain is unregistered with nothing live pending, so after `cancelChain` (HybridIndexFactory.sol:83) the same CHAINS value is proposed again; shouldListToken (174-200) proposes any coin that is not whitelisted and has no live listing, which includes a coin the guardian delisted (it is relisted at the supply in force) and a first listing the guardian cancelled. test_configureChains_skipsACoinTheFactoryWouldRefuse (test/Scripts.t.sol 1981-2044) asserts the relisting of a delisted coin as intended behaviour. Impact: a routine run of the documented `CHAIN_MODE=safe` flow silently re-proposes what the guardian vetoed, unlabelled among routine calls; the owner Safe signers must notice, and one missed 2-day veto window lists it. This is the defect RT-06 fixed for ERC-20 listings. No audit covers ConfigureChains.
proposedFix: Mirror RT-06. Add env `LIST_CHAINS` (chain ids or `all`), `LIST_COINS` (chainId:tokenId pairs or `all`) and `RELIST_COINS`, and gate the proposals: in shouldProposeChain, before `return true` for an unregistered chain: `if (registered.vault == bytes32(0) && !_contains(listChains, e.chainId)) { console2.log("skipped, a first proposal: name the chain in LIST_CHAINS", e.chainId); return false; }`; in shouldListToken after the isWhitelisted check: `uint256 inForce = f.referenceSupply(token); if (inForce == 0 && !_has(listCoins, e)) {log; return false;} if (inForce != 0 && !_has(relistCoins, e)) {log; return false;}`. Thread the lists through run/propose/safeCalldata like ConfigureWhitelist's firstListings/relist, and add tests mirroring test_RT06_aVetoedFirstListingIsNotProposedAgainByARoutineRun for chains and coins.
priorArt: RT-06, XA-11, SA-02, DA-20 (same defect class; script not covered)

title: ConfigureChains accepts a vault word of any length, and a mistyped vault is permanent (VaultFixed)
description: _word (used for both the vault and the token id) accepts any `0x` hex string of 1 to 64 digits and left-pads it. For a vault that is wrong in a plausible way, such as TRON's 21-byte hex address with its 0x41 prefix (README:144-146 requires the 20-byte address without it), a truncated address, or a 32-byte word for an EVM chain, the script builds a valid-looking proposeChain. HybridIndexFactory.proposeChain refuses a different vault for a registered chain (`VaultFixed`, HybridIndexFactory.sol:71) and nothing can unregister a chain, so once executed the chain id is bound to a word no vault has: the chain id is burned (a different vault is a different chain). Mitigations: 2-day delay, guardian/owner cancel, and the label printed in safe mode shows only the chain id. Token ids legitimately may be short (0x0), the vault word never is: vaults are 20 bytes (EVM, TRON without prefix) or 32 bytes (Solana account, NEAR/Stellar/Sui/Aptos ids).
proposedFix: script/ConfigureChains.s.sol: add `function _vaultWord(string memory raw, string memory entry) private pure returns (bytes32) { bytes32 w = _word(raw, entry); uint256 digits = bytes(raw).length - 2; if (digits != 40 && digits != 64) revert MalformedEntry(entry); return w; }` and use it in parseChains line 99 instead of `_word(f[1], parts[i])`. Add a test in test_configureChains_parse that `56:0x41<40 hex>:0x...` (42 digits) and `56:0xb5c:0x...` revert MalformedEntry (the existing test currently asserts a 3-digit vault `0x41` is accepted at line 1817-1826, which must change).

title: First-listing supply of a vault coin has no whole-unit display or plausibility bound, and a wrong first figure is near-permanent
description: For ERC-20 components the listing script logs the supply in whole tokens (ConfigureWhitelist 555-557) and the default list is bounded to 1e6..1e12 whole tokens by test (XA-24, CR-I22). For vault coins, ConfigureChains.shouldListToken checks only 0 < supply <= MAX_SUPPLY, and ConfigureWhitelist._followsPolicy (531-535) logs the raw figure in 'the chain's smallest unit'. The coins' decimals differ widely (TRX 6, XLM 7, APT 8, SUI 9, BNB/INJ/VET 18, NEAR 24), so a decimals slip is likely and invisible in the Safe batch. A first listing is bounded only by MAX_SUPPLY and review (README:473-476) and later moves are at most 0.5% a week, so a 10x error takes about 460 weekly batches to walk back and a 1000x one is effectively permanent for that token id: every index created with it carries the wrong weight, and relisting must keep the supply in force (SA-02).
proposedFix: Add a decimals field to TokenEntry (`chainId:tokenId:supply:decimals`), log `supply / 10**decimals` whole units in shouldListToken and in safe-mode labels, and skip (with the reason) outside a plausible whole-unit band, e.g. `uint256 whole = e.supply / 10**e.decimals; if (whole < 1e6 || whole > 1e12) { console2.log("skipped, implausible supply in whole units", whole); return false; }`. Add the 1e6..1e12 assertion for every shipped vault-coin entry to the fork/offline release-record test.
priorArt: XA-24, CR-I22, DA-18 (README known limitation on first listings)

title: DeployVault.checkDeployment reads back far less than its TRON and VeChain twins, so the release check cannot confirm keys, anchor, cap, floor or freezer
description: tron/deploy.mjs 326-367 and vechain/deploy.mjs 454-497 describe themselves as 'DeployVault's checkDeployment' and read back the freezer, SOURCE_CHAIN_ID, P1 PROGRAM_KEY, P2 IMAGE_ID, each verifier's anchor, anchorEpoch and GENESIS_TIME, and the native cap and floor. The Solidity original compares only p1, p2, STATE_READER, FACTORY, HUB_IMPLEMENTATION, RECOVERY_PROPOSER, SP1_VERIFIER and RISC_ZERO_VERIFIER (lines 221-228). NatSpec and README:683 say it 're-reads the wiring and the code hashes later' for the release record. After a deployment, a reviewer running it against the recorded addresses and parameters learns nothing about the freezer (a security role), the speed-limit floor and quantity cap, the P1/P2 program key and image id, or the anchor, which are exactly the values the owner and guardian must approve before proposeChain. The check inside deploy() is also tautological for these fields (the constructor arguments come from the same Params).
proposedFix: script/DeployVault.s.sol checkDeployment (lines 219-231): add `_same("freezer", p.freezer, v.freezer()); _sameWord("SOURCE_CHAIN_ID", bytes32(p.sourceChainId), bytes32(v.SOURCE_CHAIN_ID())); _sameWord("PROGRAM_KEY", p.p1ProgramKey, d.p1.PROGRAM_KEY()); _sameWord("IMAGE_ID", p.p2ImageId, d.p2.IMAGE_ID()); _sameWord("p1 anchor", p.anchor, d.p1.anchor()); _sameWord("p2 anchor", p.anchor, d.p2.anchor()); (anchorEpoch, GENESIS_TIME for both); if (v.cap(address(0)) != p.nativeCap || v.outflowFloor(address(0)) != p.nativeFloor) revert WrongWiring("native cap/floor", ...);` and extend test_deployVault_checkDeploymentRefusesAnother with a changed freezer, key, anchor and cap.

title: DeployVault accepts an anchor with one second of P1/P2 lag left; no minimum slack, unlike every DeployStateVerifier chain
description: check() refuses only `block.timestamp > lagEnds`, where lagEnds = genesis + anchorEpoch*384 + 1 day, exactly FinalityVerifier.update's own bound (FinalityVerifier.sol 87, 101-103). DeployStateVerifier gives each chain a freshness margin so the first update is still possible (MAX_ANCHOR_AGE 1h, NEAR 16h, Sui 20h, VeChain 6h, Aptos 3h, each commented 'leaves the rest of MAX_LAG to advance the verifier'). For P1 and P2 the first advance needs an SP1 and a RISC Zero proof of Ethereum finality (minutes to hours to generate) and a transaction on the vault chain; a deployment simulated with a few minutes left, and mined later, produces verifiers that 'stop for good' (README:703-704) before anyone can advance them. P1 and P2 are immutables of the vault, so the whole vault must then be redeployed. The same boundary is copied into tron/deploy.mjs 171-172 and vechain/deploy.mjs 189-190 (tron/deploy-test.mjs asserts an anchor 224 epochs old is accepted and one 226 epochs old refused, so the boundary is pinned as it is).
proposedFix: Add a slack constant and refuse inside it: `uint256 public constant MIN_ANCHOR_SLACK = 12 hours; if (block.timestamp + MIN_ANCHOR_SLACK > lagEnds) revert AnchorTooOld(p.anchorEpoch, lagEnds);` (script/DeployVault.s.sol 177), the same in tron/deploy.mjs (`(await chain.now()) + 43_200n > lagEnds`) and vechain/deploy.mjs, and move test_LG4_deployVaultRefusesAnAnchorTheVerifiersCannotAdvance (test/Scripts.t.sol 1568-1586) and tron/deploy-test.mjs's 224/226-epoch cases to the new boundary.

title: Owner check is Safe-only and fail-open: any other contract (a 1-of-1 smart account, a forwarder to a hot key) is accepted without a threshold or module check
description: checkOwner enforces 'at least 3 signatures and no module' only when the owner answers getThreshold() with one word; otherwise it accepts the contract 'as it is' (lines 194-203; test_L06_checkOwner asserts SilentFallback and a router are accepted). The documented rule (AGENTS.md 'Deployment rules', README:656-659) is phrased for a Safe, but the design rule behind it is a 3-of-5 owner. Any ERC-4337/Argent/Coinbase-style single-owner account, an Ownable executor or a Safe-like contract with a different ABI is an accepted owner on mainnet, and a Safe whose getThreshold call reverts is treated like a timelock. The owner has no power over funds but proposes every listing, supply batch and guardian change; the Safe-only rule is what stops a single key holding them. Because the OWNER value is operator input this guards mistakes, not a hostile operator; the ownership transfer path (Ownable2Step, no delay) has no equivalent check at all.
proposedFix: script/Deploy.s.sol: in the else-branch of lines 197-202 take the restrictive path unless the operator acknowledges a non-Safe owner explicitly: `if (!(ok && data.length == 32)) { if (!vm.envOr("OWNER_IS_NOT_A_SAFE_ACK", false)) revert OwnerNotASafe(owner); return; }`, and print the acknowledged owner's code hash in the deploy log. Add `error OwnerNotASafe(address owner);` and update test_L06_checkOwner/test_CRI36_aFailedSafeCallIsNeverReadAsAnAnswer accordingly (a Safe whose getThreshold reverts must be refused, not accepted).

title: The vault's recovery proposer is only required to be 'a contract' (or two TRON keys): no threshold or module check, unlike the factory owner
description: RECOVERY_PROPOSER is the owner's emergency multisig that, once a vault has stalled, proposes a successor verifier pair that nobody but the freezer (2 vetoes per stall) can stop for 30 days (design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-b-spec.md 545-560). A successor pair is its own code and attests its own continuity proofs, so the proposer's security is the vault's last line under a stall. checkRoles requires only `code.length != 0` and no 0xef01 prefix (lines 212-213); vechain/deploy.mjs 222-230 is identical; tron/deploy.mjs 203-224 requires an owner and active permissions with at least two keys and no single key reaching the threshold. A 1-of-1 Safe, a Safe with modules, or any wallet contract passes, although Deploy.checkOwner applies the 3-signature and no-module rule to the factory owner whose power is smaller (data, behind a delay and a veto). The same would let one hot key act as the 'multisig'.
proposedFix: Factor Deploy.checkOwner's Safe rules into ScriptUtils (`checkMultisig(address)`, using ISafeThreshold: threshold >= 3, no modules, not the broadcaster or the freezer among getOwners) and call it from DeployVault.checkRoles for the recovery proposer, with the same explicit acknowledgement for non-Safe contracts as proposed for the owner; mirror in vechain/deploy.mjs (read getThreshold/getModulesPaginated through chain.view) and raise tron/deploy.mjs's isMultisig minimum from two keys to three. Add tests in test_deployVault_refusals for a threshold-1 Safe and a Safe with a module.

title: TRON and VeChain deploy tools deploy gitignored build output with no freshness check, record no source commit, and have no resume or balance check
description: deploy.mjs for TRON reads tron/out/<name>.json (art(), line 262), produced by a separate `npm run build` into a gitignored folder (.gitignore '/tron/out/'); VeChain's reads out/ and vechain/out/ (ARTIFACTS, vechain/deploy.mjs 236-245). Nothing checks that the artifact was built from the current, committed tree: a stale out/ from an earlier source revision is deployed and its code hash printed with no link to a commit. forge script records the git commit in broadcast/<script>/<chain>/run-latest.json and README:666-669 tells operators to broadcast from a clean committed tree; the JS record (tron/deploy.mjs 411-413, vechain/deploy.mjs 554-555) prints only {network, chainId, address, codehash}. Other hazards in the same paths: tron/deploy.mjs 281 treats a missing receipt.result as SUCCESS (`r.receipt?.result ??
