'SUCCESS'`), tron has no deployer balance check (VeChain does, 543-547) although a deployment costs about 1,220 TRX across seven transactions, and neither tool can resume: after a failure at transaction N the earlier contracts exist and a re-run deploys everything again (VeChain additionally leaves every created contract with the deployer as Prototype master until the last transaction clears them, 441-444). tron/build.mjs 44 discards the compiler's stderr (`stdio: ['ignore','pipe','ignore']`), so a failed build shows no error and leaves the previous out/ in place.
proposedFix: In both deploy.mjs: before sending, run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` and refuse a dirty tree; compare each artifact's `source` hash with a freshly built one (have deploy.mjs call build.mjs, or store sha256 of the sources in out/<name>.json at build time and recompute it); add `commit`, `dirty` and compiler version to the printed record. tron/deploy.mjs 281: `if (r.receipt?.result !== 'SUCCESS') throw ...` (no default). Add a `--resume <record.json>` that skips contracts whose address already has the expected code hash, a TRX balance pre-check using `fee-limit * 7`, and for VeChain clear each master in the same transaction as its creation or on failure. tron/build.mjs 44: `stdio: ['ignore','pipe','inherit']`.

title: Repo.t.sol tests named for a CI claim pass without it (XA-10, I11, I09), contradicting the rule that a regression test must fail without its fix
description: (a) test_XA10_ciRunsEveryGate ('CI runs every gate of the definition of done') asserts lint, coverage, the secret condition and Wake, but never `forge fmt --check`, `forge build --sizes` or `forge test` (grep of the file finds none): deleting the fmt, build or test step of .github/workflows/test.yml leaves every Repo test green, although AGENTS.md says CI enforces items 1 to 5. (b) test_I11_theCiToolchainIsPinned asserts `_contains(workflow, "MAINNET_RPC_URL")`, but the name occurs in the 'Require the fork-test RPC' step too, so removing `env: MAINNET_RPC_URL: ${{ secrets.MAINNET_RPC_URL }}` from the test step (silently skipping the four fork suites) still passes. (c) test_I09_theKnownLimitationsAreDocumented asserts the phrase 'Known limitations' appears anywhere in README.md; README.md:206 contains it in a sentence ('see "Known limitations"'), so deleting the whole section at README.md:451 passes. AGENTS.md: 'A regression test has to fail without its fix.'
proposedFix:
test/Repo.t.sol: in test_XA10 add `assertTrue(_contains(workflow, "run: forge fmt --check")); assertTrue(_contains(workflow, "run: forge build --sizes")); assertTrue(_contains(workflow, "run: forge test -vvv"));`; in test_I11 require the test step's env block `assertTrue(_contains(workflow, "run: forge test -vvv
        env:
          MAINNET_RPC_URL: ${{ secrets.MAINNET_RPC_URL }}"));`; in test_I09 `assertTrue(_contains(readme, "
## Known limitations
"))` and assert at least N bullet lines follow. Verify each against a mutant (delete the step / the section) before relying on it.

title: The test guarding the central 'no price in any contract' rule is a five-word blacklist
description: AGENTS.md says `test_noContractReadsAPrice` 'fails if src/ or abi/ names an oracle or a pool's price'. It searches src/ and abi/ for exactly five strings: latestRoundData, AggregatorV3, slot0, observe(, navPerToken (line 210). Common ways to read a price pass: Chainlink `latestAnswer`/`getRoundData`, Uniswap V4 `getSlot0` (capital S, so 'slot0' does not match) or an `extsload` of a pool slot, V2 `getReserves`, any quoter or TWAP `consult(`, Pyth `getPrice`. The tree is clean today (I grepped src/ and abi/ for these and found none), so this is a guard that would not trip, for the design's first rule.
proposedFix: test/Repo.t.sol line 210: widen to `string[12] memory priceWords = ["latestRoundData", "latestAnswer", "getRoundData", "AggregatorV3", "slot0", "Slot0", "observe(", "getReserves", "sqrtPriceX96", "consult(", "getPrice", "navPerToken"];` (and the helper's parameter type), and add a self-test that the scanner trips on a string written to a temp fixture under the allowed fs path.

title: README tells operators two signers sign the Safe batch; the owner Safe must need at least three
description: README.md:813-814: 'In the Safe app, a safe mode's output becomes one Transaction Builder batch ... Two signers sign it, and one executes it.' README.md:656-659, AGENTS.md ('Deployment rules'), ARCHITECTURE.md:508 and Deploy.MIN_OWNER_THRESHOLD require a Safe of at least three signatures on mainnet (the owner's call of 2026-09-30); a 2-of-N Safe is refused (test_L06_checkOwner). The sentence is a leftover of the old two-signature rule and misdescribes the runbook the operators follow for every weekly batch.
proposedFix: README.md line 814: replace 'Two signers sign it, and one executes it.' with 'At least three of the Safe's signers sign it (the owner Safe's threshold), and one executes it.'

title: initialize pins neither P1/P2's identity nor DeployVault's role checks: a finalized stub verifier is accepted as a mainnet P1/P2, and the freezer may be the deployer key
description: I was asked to verify that nothing in src/ or script/ names the stub and that the vault cannot be pointed at it in production. The first holds: no file in src/ or script/ names stub-verifier. The second does not. `handle_initialize` (setup.rs:53-80) accepts any two distinct executable programs that pass `check_immutable` (vault.rs:184-206). `stub-verifier` passes once its authority is removed, and solana/README.md:115-116 tells the deployer to do exactly that ('Make each stub final'). Rotation (governance.rs:59-67) and the successor (recovery.rs:112-121) also accept any immutable program. For the EVM, the guard is in script/DeployVault.s.sol:170-213. It refuses any Groth16 verifier but the pinned SP1 and RISC Zero ones, requires the P1 program key, the P2 image id and a fresh anchor, refuses floor > cap, and requires a freezer that is neither the broadcaster nor the recovery proposer. The Solana side has no equivalent. There is no production deploy script; the only tooling is `demo/relayer`'s `solana-init`, which is devnet-only and wires stubs. `initialize` itself checks only that recovery_proposer is off-curve and differs from the freezer. Consequences: (a) a vault initialized with stubs, or with verifiers holding a wrong program key or anchor, looks identical on Ethereum. The factory registers only the 32-byte config key, so anyone holding a stub's relayer key can forge any burn. (b) `freezer == authority` (the broadcasting key) and `native_floor > native_cap` are accepted. Nothing in this is hidden, since the config and the programs are public, but a deployment slip in this direction is silent. Mitigation: Solana cannot launch until its state verifier exists (it waits on Alpenglow).
priorArt: SOL-1, SOL-2 (stub initialization and verifier immutability; the identity pin was never added)

title: Deposits are taken before the first checkpoint; if none ever arrives they can never be settled, refunded or exited
description: `initialize` seeds the checkpoint as {block: 0, timestamp: now, state_root: 0} (setup.rs:121-125), which buys a week of grace, and `deposit` checks only frozen and stalled (deposits.rs:51-57). So deposits are taken while no checkpoint exists. If no checkpoint is ever proven, those deposits are unrecoverable. This happens if P1 or P2 is initialized with a wrong program key or anchor, or if neither is advanced within MAX_LAG of its anchor, after which it 'stops for good' (LG-4). (a) INTAKE_SETTLED and INTAKE_FAILED need both proofs and `block <= checkpoint.block = 0` (messages.rs:269, vault.rs:124-130), which no message satisfies. The hub's permissionless `failIntake` sends INTAKE_FAILED, but it can never run here. (b) A rotation is also a loosening message, so it cannot run either. (c) `propose_successor` must prove the zero checkpoint with both new verifiers (recovery.rs:125-126). No honest verifier proves block 0 with a zero state root. (d) `begin_snapshot` refuses NoCheckpoint (recovery.rs:245). So the SOL deposited in the grace week stays in `held` for good. The spec's own reason for refusing deposits while stalled (spec 5.6: 'it may never see the message that would settle or refund it') applies equally before the first checkpoint. XindexVault.deposit (lines 176-180) has the same gap. Per the twin rule the fix belongs in every vault.

title: A CAP_UPDATE whose cap or floor exceeds u64 can never be delivered to the Solana vault, though an EVM vault would apply it
description: `read_cap` converts the cap and the floor with `to_u64`, which returns Overflow above 2^64-1 (governance.rs:112-115, core abi.rs:41-46). The factory's `proposeCap(chainId, token, cap, floor)` (HybridIndexFactory.sol:165-170) takes uint256 and has no idea of a chain's amount width. An EVM vault stores any uint256, and NEAR's uses u128. So an owner who proposes a large cap for Solana (for example 1e20 lamports, or type(uint256).max as 'unlimited') waits LISTING_DELAY and executes, and the vault then rejects the message on every delivery attempt (`handle_deliver_governance` reverts at line 482). The cap stays at its old value with no on-chain signal. If the same message also lowers the floor, that protective lowering never applies either. The nonce is not consumed, so a later message still works. Because a lamport amount always fits u64, any value above u64::MAX means the same as u64::MAX here, so refusing the message protects nothing.

title: Snapshot-claim EIP-712 domain uses the registry's chain id, which common wallets refuse to sign
description: A holder with no registered recovery key can leave a stalled Solana vault only by signing `SnapshotClaim` with its Ethereum key (exit.rs:96-105). The domain is `EIP712Domain(string name,string version,uint256 chainId,bytes32 salt)`, and its chainId is the factory registry's id for Solana (`config.chain_id`, snapshot.rs:233; the demo uses 1,399,811,150). MetaMask's eth_signTypedData_v4 refuses a typed-data request whose domain.chainId differs from the active network ('Provided chainId ... must match the active chainId'). Several other wallets enforce the same rule. No EVM network carries the registry's id for Solana, so a holder on a mainstream wallet cannot produce the signature without hand-built tooling, such as a custom RPC that reports that chain id, or `cast wallet sign --data`. This is the last-resort exit, reached 180 days into a stall, and it is the only path for every holder that did not register a recovery key. Replay protection would not need the registry id. The salt is the vault's unique 32-byte id, and the domain and struct typehashes differ from the EVM vault's.

title: Vault::build omits DeployVault's guards: floor above cap (speed limit never binds) and source chain equal to the vault's own chain
description: AGENTS.md: DeployVault refuses 'the indexes' own chain' and 'a floor above the cap' (script/DeployVault.s.sol:96,180 `FloorAboveCap`). `Vault::build` (the only place NEAR's initial config is checked, as `new` or as the NEP-616 initial data) checks factory, hub implementation, recovery proposer, P1/P2 and their distinct systems, but not `native_floor <= native_cap` and not `source_chain_id != chain_id`. `speed::available_wide` is `max(4% of (balance+recent), floor) - recent` (speed.rs:61-65), so a floor above any realistic balance makes the 4%/day limit non-binding: one delivered (even forged) burn can pay the whole index balance at once, breaking design invariant I5. A deterministic account has no later chance to fix it (no owner); a CAP_UPDATE can lower it only through the factory's 2-day + 7-day path, and the vault never checks floor<=cap there either (same on the EVM: HybridIndexFactory.proposeCap, line 165-170, does not check it). Impact: a mis-set config registered after a hurried review removes the key safety limit. Mitigation: review.

title: Initial checkpoint timestamp is a deployer-chosen `now` in the NEP-616 path; a far-future value permanently blocks every checkpoint, intake settle/fail and any stall recovery
description: `Vault::build(config, now)` seeds `checkpoint.timestamp = now` as the first week's stall grace (the EVM uses block.timestamp, which cannot be in the future). In the NEP-616 path `now` is an argument of the off-chain initial-state computation (sandbox.rs:329 passes `real_time - 1_000`); nothing bounds it. `checkpoint::is_newer` requires `c.timestamp > last.timestamp`, so with `now` far in the future (a typo, a ms/ns mix-up: the contract itself divides ns by 1e9, lib.rs:150) no real Ethereum block is ever newer: `advance_checkpoint` always fails NotNewer; every index message is `loosening` and needs `block <= checkpoint.block (0)` -> NotCheckpointed (lib.rs:369-374), including INTAKE_SETTLED/FAILED, so deposited NEAR can neither be credited nor refunded; `stalled()` stays false until that date, so no successor and no snapshot exit is reachable. The account is keyless and immutable, so the deposits are locked for good. The opposite error (a past `now`, or P1/P2 anchors older than MAX_LAG at the time of the first update_verifier) merely starts the vault stalled/dead: `check_lag` refuses updates, deposits revert VaultStalled, until the account is replaced, harmless before any deposit but undetectable on chain. Deposits are only possible while not stalled, so the lock needs the vault registered with the bad `now`.
proposedFix:
crates/xindex-core/src/checkpoint.rs is_newer, and a NEAR-only wrapper: treat the first checkpoint specially so the baked grace time cannot block it:
-        && c.timestamp > last.timestamp
+        && (last.block == 0 || c.timestamp > last.timestamp)
(this changes only the genesis grace case, where `last.state_root` is zero; port the same line to the EVM vault `_checkNewer`, Solana, Stellar in one change to keep the twins aligned). Alternatively leave the code and make the verification tool of B2-01 refuse a `now` more than one hour from the block time of the creating transaction.

title: Stellar vault constructor never binds `chain_id` / `source_chain_id` to the network, and no script/test covers a Stellar deployment (HUB-I2 left to a manual step)
description: HUB-I2 ('a chain's registry id must equal its vault's chain id, which messages and digests both carry; a deployment check for every vault chain') is enforced for EVM chains by `DeployVault.s.sol`, but a Stellar vault goes up with `stellar contract deploy` (README 'Deploying' step 2) and its constructor stores `args.chain_id` and `args.source_chain_id` unchecked (lib.rs:86-89). With the vault immutable and ownerless, a wrong id (testnet's 17667989177921016935 on pubnet, a typo, 0) is irreversible: every message fails `WrongRoute`, every intake digest differs from what the hub expects, so the hub can never prove a deposit and the vault can never receive `INTAKE_FAILED`; depositors' XLM then stays locked until a 7-day stall plus the 180-day snapshot exit. The same manual-deployment gap covers the other EVM deployment rules in AGENTS.md (freezer not the broadcasting key, recovery proposer a non-delegated contract, non-zero factory/template): the constructor can check some (they are), but nothing automated or tested exercises a Stellar deployment end to end. `env.ledger().network_id()` is available inside the constructor, so the chain/network pairing can be enforced on chain.
priorArt: HUB-I2 (documented as a deployment check for every vault chain)

title: Stellar statement's quorum-set sanity check accepts any non-zero threshold, so a weak pinned set would yield a weak verifier instead of a dead one
description: `StellarStateVerifier` pins only the SHA-256 of the quorum set; nobody can decode it on chain, and `DeployStateVerifier.deployStellar` hashes whatever XDR it is given (script/DeployStateVerifier.s.sol:323-343). The only guard against a mistaken pin is `quorum::check_sane`, which runs inside the zkVM program but only refuses depth > 4, duplicate validators, and `threshold == 0 || threshold > members` (quorum.rs:29-31). Its own doc says it 'guards against a mistaken pin'. A set with threshold 1 of 10 organisations, or an organisation level with 1 of 3 validators, passes, and the resulting verifier then trusts any single organisation (or one validator key) to forge an `attest` of any vault state, which lets a forged deposit proof mint index shares (bounded only by the hub's 4%/day mint cap). Because the program key is fixed, a stricter check inside the program would turn such a mispin into a verifier no proof can satisfy (fail closed), which is the safer failure. Today's real Tier 1 (7 of 10 organisations, 2 of 3 validators each) satisfies a two-thirds rule.

title: The Stellar zk program's key (StellarStateVerifier.PROGRAM_KEY) has no reproducible-build recipe and no re-derivation check
description: PROGRAM_KEY is a derived constant that gates every proof the verifier accepts. It is the verifying-key hash of the ELF built by `sp1_build::build_program("../program")` (script/build.rs:3), a plain local build with the SP1 toolchain installed by `sp1up` (version not pinned by the repo; `proofs/stellar/rust-toolchain` is the floating `stable` for the host), no Docker/`--locked`/path-remapping. SP1 guest ELFs embed panic-location paths and depend on the exact toolchain, so two honest builders can derive different keys, and a reviewer cannot confirm that the key deployed in `StellarStateVerifier` is the audited statement. `DeployStateVerifier.deployStellar` takes `programKey` from a JSON file unchecked (test/fixtures/stellar/anchor.json holds a test key only), and nothing in CI or tests recomputes it (the spec only plans a reproducible build for P2's image id: Stage B spec section 11, ARCHITECTURE.md:962). Impact: a wrong or non-reproducible key is either a dead verifier (liveness) or, if the deployer uses a key from a different program, a verifier trusting different code; both are only caught by manual review.
proposedFix: proofs/stellar/script/build.rs: build the guest reproducibly, e.g. `sp1_build::build_program_with_args("../program", sp1_build::BuildArgs { docker: true, tag: "v6.8.1".into(), ..Default::default() })`, commit the expected key in `proofs/stellar/PROGRAM_KEY` (and for the measurement binary state that its key is never deployed), print it in `stellar-proof vkey`, and add a CI/release step that rebuilds and compares. In `script/DeployStateVerifier.s.sol::deployStellar` require the key to equal the committed one (or log it prominently next to the quorum-set hash for reviewers).
priorArt: Stage B spec section 11 (P2 image id reproducibility); applies equally to P1 and the other SP1 state proofs

title: Sui vault's immutability is an unenforced manual step the Ethereum verifier cannot detect (PACKAGE_ID is the type-origin id, which survives upgrades)
description: vault.move's header states as fact 'No owner, no upgrade, no capability: the package is made immutable in its publishing transaction', and design/2026-10-04-four-chains-interfaces.md says the same. Nothing in the repo performs or checks that step: sui/ has no publish script (README gives prose only: 'Check on chain that the package's UpgradeCap is gone'), and `vault::create` / `SuiStateVerifier` cannot see it. On Sui a type's address is the package id in which the type was FIRST defined, and an upgrade keeps it. So if the publisher keeps the UpgradeCap, it can later upgrade `vault` (any public function body may change under the compatible policy: `deliver`, `pay`, `attest`), operate on the same shared `Vault`, and still produce objects of type `<PACKAGE_ID>::vault::Attestation`, which `SuiStateVerifier.verifySlots` (MODULE 'vault', NAME 'Attestation', package = PACKAGE_ID) accepts unchanged. Impact if the step is skipped or done wrongly: the vault is no longer ownerless (funds and every Ethereum-side evidence rule rest on the deployer's key), and Ethereum has no way to notice. Preconditions: a deployer mistake or a malicious deployer, and the owner's 2-day listing review missing it. The Aptos twin is better placed (`upgrade_policy = "immutable"` is in Move.toml and visible in 0x1::code::PackageRegistry); Sui has no equivalent flag, so the control is purely procedural. Rated LOW because the README does require the check and it is verifiable from the publish transaction's effects (UpgradeCap deleted).
proposedFix: 1) sui/README.md, section 'Ownerless and immutable' (lines ~115-123): add a mandatory gate and an exact recipe. Before: 'Check on chain that the package's `UpgradeCap` is gone'. After: 'A Sui vault may be registered (`proposeChain`) only after the publish transaction's effects (`sui client tx-block <digest>`) show the `UpgradeCap` object deleted and the package object immutable; record the digest in the listing proposal's notes. Publish with one PTB: `--publish .` assigned to `cap`, then `--move-call 0x2::package::make_immutable cap`.' 2) design/2026-10-04-four-chains-interfaces.md Sui bullet: add 'Ethereum cannot verify this; the registry review must.' 3) src/verifiers/SuiStateVerifier.sol NatSpec above PACKAGE_ID (line 73): add `/// @dev The package's ORIGINAL id: also the address of the Attestation type after any upgrade, so a surviving UpgradeCap would not change what this verifier accepts; immutability is a deployment fact it cannot check.` 4) Optionally add the digest check to ConfigureChains' pre-flight documentation (script/ConfigureChains.s.sol header).
priorArt: none (SOL-2 is the EVM-side analogue, handled by construction there)

title: Solana prototype: written_state returns a zero-lamport account whose data and owner are unauthenticated
description: account_lt_hash (lthash.rs 73-77) maps any account with lamports == 0 to the identity hash, so a write entry {pubkey: V, old: None, new: Some(Account{lamports: 0, data: ATTACKER, owner: VAULT_PROGRAM, ..})} contributes nothing to the lattice sum. apply_writes therefore still equals the slot's accounts_lt_hash whenever the real writes of the slot are listed, and written_state (lines 101-104) then returns Some(&fake) for V although V was not written in that slot (or does not exist at all). Scenario: a prover lists the real writes of a finalized slot in which the vault account was NOT touched, plus the fake zero-lamport entry for the vault; the check passes and the 'proven' state is attacker-chosen bytes. The only safeguard is that the caller must additionally reject lamports == 0; the function's doc ('Returns the state `pubkey` was written to') and the module doc ('so the vault's account written in that slot is proven') do not say so, and design/2026-10-03-solana-state-proof.md section 2 records the identity rule but not this consequence. Nothing is exploitable today (the Ethereum verifier and the zkVM statement are not built), but the statement author will build on this API. Same for a zero-lamport `old`. The legitimate vault always holds rent-exempt lamports, so rejecting zero costs nothing.
proposedFix:
proofs/solana-state/src/bank.rs lines 101-104, replace
    Ok(writes.iter().find(|w| w.pubkey == *pubkey).and_then(|w| w.new.as_ref()))
with
    Ok(writes.iter().find(|w| w.pubkey == *pubkey).and_then(|w| w.new.as_ref()).filter(|a| a.lamports > 0))
and in apply_writes reject (DeltaError::ZeroLamport(pubkey)) any Write whose old/new is Some with lamports == 0 (a zero-lamport state is 'None' by definition). Add a test in tests/state.rs: a slot whose real writes exclude pubkey V, plus Write{pubkey: V, old: None, new: Some(zero-lamport account with data)}; assert written_state(...) is Err or Ok(None), never Ok(Some(_)).
priorArt: none; design/2026-10-03-solana-state-proof.md section 4 item 5 covers LtHash collision resistance but not the identity rule

title: Aptos statement: derived domain constants UPDATE, SLOTS, ATTEST_DOMAIN are hex literals with no Rust test that recomputes them, and hex32 ignores trailing characters
description: UPDATE, SLOTS and ATTEST_DOMAIN are keccak256 of 'xindex.v4.aptos.update', 'xindex.v4.aptos.slots', 'xindex.v4.vault-attest' written as hex strings parsed by a const fn hex32 that reads exactly the first 64 hex characters and never asserts the string length (a longer literal is silently truncated; a shorter one fails to compile). I recomputed all three with cast keccak and they match today (0x11b68bff..., 0xf7afe75b..., 0xb0ec2b25...). But proofs/aptos/statement/tests/statement.rs has no test that recomputes them (grep for UPDATE/SLOTS/ATTEST_DOMAIN in it finds none); they are only exercised indirectly through the Python-generated public values (generate.py recomputes them with its own keccak) and through test/AptosStateVerifier.t.sol. The twin crate proofs/vechain does have the direct test (statement/tests/statement.rs 27-33). These words gate which claim a proof makes (update vs slots) and the record's domain, so a typo in a later edit would be caught only if the fixtures are regenerated with the same typo.

title: Vault rule constants shared by six vault implementations are pinned to Solidity by no test
description: Extracted every cross-vault rule constant from XindexVault.sol (25-39), crates/xindex-core/src/constants.rs (8-25, shared by the Solana, NEAR and Stellar vaults), sui/sources/vault.move (101-112), aptos/sources/vault.move (111-122) and the docs (README, ARCHITECTURE 741-779, AGENTS 452-461, stage-B spec 131-153/535-569). TODAY ALL AGREE: SPEED_LIMIT 4% (0.04e18 == x*4/100, same floor), 25 hourly buckets, FREEZE_DURATION 14d, GOVERNANCE_DELAY 7d, MAX_INTAKE_LIFE 7d, STALL_PERIOD 7d, RECOVERY_DELAY 30d, MAX_RECOVERY_VETOES 2, SNAPSHOT_EXIT_DELAY 180d (stall_start + delay in every vault, `>=` in all), message kinds 1..8, intake states 0..3, DOMAIN / EVENT_TOPIC / INDEX_DIGEST_DOMAIN / INTAKE_DIGEST_DOMAIN / VAULT_TOKEN_DOMAIN / EIP-712 hashes / ATTEST_DOMAIN (all 37 keccak-derived literals recomputed with cast: match), deadline_of = top 64 bits (shift 192) in Solidity, Rust and both Move twins. The hazard is that nothing keeps them equal. The Rust core's duration/limit constants are only ever tested against themselves: solana tests/vault.rs:572,776, near src/tests/governance.rs:24,33 and recovery.rs:134, stellar tests/vault.rs:659 all assert `now + FREEZE_DURATION` / `GOVERNANCE_DELAY` / `RECOVERY_DELAY` using the constant imported from xindex_core::constants, so editing constants.rs (say FREEZE_DURATION to 15 days, or SPEED_LIMIT_PERCENT to 5) keeps every Solana/NEAR/Stellar test green. crates/xindex-core/tests/vault.rs `the_constants_are_their_hashes` pins only the keccak domains, not the numbers. Sui/Aptos tests re-declare the literals locally (sui/tests/recovery_tests.move:13-15, governance_tests.move:17-18), which pins each Move vault to the literal but not to Solidity. The Solidity side pins XindexVault to literals (test/XindexVault.t.sol:166-167) but never reads the other implementations. Only the 'aptos/tests/fixtures/mutants.py' mutant runner mentions SPEED_LIMIT_PERCENT. A change to one vault's rule (a safety rule: speed limit, freeze, review delay) can therefore land on one chain only, which AGENTS.md ('A change to either vault's rules or to a message goes into both') makes a pure convention. Inside Solidity the duplicates (FREEZE 14d in HybridHubStorage.FREEZE_LENGTH, HybridIndexFactory.FREEZE_DURATION and XindexVault.FREEZE_DURATION; MINT_LIMIT and SPEED_LIMIT both 0.04e18; BUCKETS/HOUR/digest domains in HybridHubStorage and XindexVault) are each pinned to the same literal by tests (HybridHub.t.sol:773-774, HybridIndexFactory.t.sol:45, XindexVault.t.sol:166-167), so no gap there.
priorArt: none (AGENTS.md 'Stage B' twin rule; VLT-2, LG-4)

title: Governance and settlement message bodies (CAP_UPDATE, FREEZER_CHANGE, VERIFIER_ROTATION, FREEZE, INTAKE_SETTLED/FAILED) have no Solidity-generated cross-language pin
description: The cross-language encoding pins are: the envelope and a real BURN payload (core tests/vault.rs `a_burn_decodes`, hard-coded cast-abi-encode hex), the index/intake digests (`digests_match_solidity`), the clone address, the hub storage reads and EIP-712 claim digest against five committed hub.json captures (burn, migrate, settled/open intake proofs), and Move's `abi_tests.move` (`a_message_decodes_as_solidity_encodes_it`, `the_hubs_own_messages_decode`, `the_digests_and_slots_are_soliditys`) plus sui/aptos tests/fixtures/vectors.py. No test pins the body layout of the other kinds against bytes Solidity produced: each non-EVM vault's tests build those payloads with their own encoder (solana tests/common/mod.rs:824 `payload`, near src/tests/encode.rs:16 `message` and governance.rs `cap_body`, stellar tests/common/mod.rs:474), so a vault and its tests can agree with each other and disagree with the hub/factory. I checked the decoders by reading: CAP_UPDATE (token, cap, floor) is read at words 0/1/2 by Solidity (XindexVault.sol:339,401), Solana (governance.rs:111-116) and Sui (vault.move:959-962) - they agree today; FREEZER_CHANGE, VERIFIER_ROTATION and INTAKE_* bodies were not re-read in every vault. A transposition would be liveness-breaking at best (messages refused) and, for CAP_UPDATE (cap vs floor swap) or a rotation's p1/p2 order, could apply a different loosening than the factory authorised on that chain only. Severity LOW because decoders are one-line word reads and I found no disagreement.
proposedFix: Extend hub.json generation (each tests/fixtures/generate.py) or add a Solidity-side `vm.writeJson` of one canonical payload per kind (VaultMessages.encode of CAP_UPDATE with token=0,cap=500e18,floor=0.5e18; FREEZER_CHANGE; VERIFIER_ROTATION with two distinct words; FREEZE; INTAKE_SETTLED; INTAKE_FAILED) into test/fixtures/vault-messages.json, and add one test per implementation that decodes each and asserts kind, destChain, nonce and every body word. Minimal Rust variant for crates/xindex-core/tests/vault.rs: const CAP_PAYLOAD: &str = '<cast abi-encode output>'; let m = decode_message(&hex(CAP_PAYLOAD)).unwrap(); assert_eq!(m.kind, CAP_UPDATE); assert_eq!(*body_word(m.body,3,1).unwrap(), word(500e18)); assert_eq!(*body_word(m.body,3,2).unwrap(), word(0.5e18)); and the same for the other kinds; Move: copy the vectors into sui/tests/abi_tests.move and aptos/tests/abi_tests.move.
priorArt: none (AGENTS.md claims 'abi tests pin every encoding')

title: AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md say the Solana program's `abi` tests pin every encoding against Solidity; no such tests exist there
description: AGENTS.md:474 ('The Solana vault is the EVM vault's twin ... its `abi` tests pin every encoding against Solidity's') and ARCHITECTURE.md:790 repeat the claim. solana/programs/xindex-vault/src/abi.rs (87 lines) is a re-export of xindex_core::abi with no tests, and solana/programs/xindex-vault/tests/ holds exit.rs, real_verifiers.rs, recovery.rs and vault.rs only. The pins moved to crates/xindex-core/tests/vault.rs when the shared core was extracted, and they cover the envelope, BURN, MIGRATE, the digests and the hub storage reads, not 'every encoding' (see C1-02). A future session trusting the sentence will not add a pin when it adds a message kind or changes a body.
proposedFix: AGENTS.md:474 and ARCHITECTURE.md:790: replace 'its `abi` tests pin every encoding against Solidity's' with 'the shared core's tests (`crates/xindex-core/tests/vault.rs`) pin the message envelope, BURN and MIGRATE bodies, both digests and the snapshot reads against Solidity's; a new message kind needs its own pin there'.

title: CI runs Foundry only: no cargo, Move, npm or Anchor gate runs for the six non-EVM vaults, the shared core or the proof statements
description: The only workflow (test.yml, one job 'Foundry project') runs submodule check, forge fmt/build/lint/test/coverage, the ABI regenerate-and-diff and `wake detect all src`. AGENTS.md lists many gates for crates/xindex-core, solana/, near/, stellar/, sui/, aptos/, proofs/* and vechain/ (cargo test/fmt/clippy, cargo build-sbf, sui move test, aptos move test, npm run deploy-test) as conventions ('Run everything locally'), none enforced. Every cross-language pin in C1-01/C1-02 and the five hub.json fixtures are consumed only by those unrun suites. Scenario: a PR edits crates/xindex-core/src/speed.rs or constants.rs (shared by Solana, NEAR and Stellar vaults that custody funds) and breaks or loosens a rule; forge-only CI is green and merges. Also no `cargo --locked`/lockfile-diff check, so Cargo.lock drift (e.g. sha2 0.9.9/0.10.8/0.10.9/0.11.0 coexisting in solana/ and near/ locks) is invisible. Severity LOW because the owner runs the gates locally by convention; the orchestrator may raise it given these vaults hold funds.
proposedFix: Add jobs to .github/workflows/test.yml (path-filtered if desired): core: `cd crates/xindex-core && cargo test --locked && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo build --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features`; near/stellar/solana/proofs: the gates AGENTS.md lists, each with --locked; sui: `sui move build && sui move test` with the keyless SUI_CONFIG_DIR; aptos: `aptos move compile --dev --fail-on-warning && aptos move test --dev`. Until then reword AGENTS.md 'CI enforces items 1 to 5' to say the Stage B gates are not in CI.

title: Hub/vault storage slots are copied into three Solidity files, the Rust core, two Move modules and five fixture generators, pinned only by a Solidity test and by five hub.json captures that carry no source revision

Reverts AlreadyListed for a\n///         whitelisted token, whose supply changes only in a batch, and TokenInBatch while `token` is in the live\n///         supply batch. An expired proposal can be proposed again.'

title: Zap burn sells the previewed redeem amounts instead of measuring what redeem delivered
description: AGENTS.md (zap 'Checks') requires the zap to 'measure what the user pays and receives as balance changes inside the call, never using tokens already in the zap', and the IndexZap header (46-47) says tokens already sitting in the zap 'are never used'. _burnBasket instead takes `got = previewRedeem(shares)` (239) and sells exactly got[i] of each component (_sellV3 / _sellV4 pre-fund the router with got[i], 323 and 343), on the comment that redeem 'rounds down deterministically, so the preview is the exact amount received' (238). That holds only while every component transfers exactly what it is asked to. IndexHub.issue explicitly guards the opposite case 'even if a whitelisted token changes behaviour' (IndexHub.sol:158-161), but the zap's burn does not: if a listed component (for example an upgradeable proxy token listed later) began charging a transfer fee or rounding down transfers (stETH-style 1-2 wei), redeem would deliver less than got[i], and `token.safeTransfer(ROUTER, got[i])` would draw the difference from whatever balance of that token the zap holds (strays someone left there) and pay it to the burner, or revert when the zap holds none. Impact is small (only stray balances, which are lost funds anyway, or a revert that sends users to redeem directly), and the whitelist policy excludes such tokens, so this is a hazard: the code relies on an unenforced token property where the documented rule says it measures.
priorArt: none (CR-L02 covered router strays; XA/DA zap reviews covered pass-through and zero legs)

title: HUB-2 covers only an empty index: a residual dust supply keeps an index mint-dead and its creator cannot re-seed it
description: HUB-2's rationale is that a dust supply never grows under 4% a day, so only the creator may seed, and only when supply == 0 (line 297). The same dead end is reached when an index empties but for dust: with supply = 1 wei, _mintRoom = floor(1 * 0.04e18 / 1e18) = 0, so nobody can settle an order or accept a migration, and the creator's exemption does not apply because supply != 0. Scenario: holders of an index redeem or migrate away; a stranger keeps (or buys) 1 wei of shares and never redeems it. The index can never mint again, and its creator cannot revive it, until that wei is burned; with a supply of 1e15 the cap would need about 400 days to reach one share. Residual dust (AMM positions, MintRequests escrows, rounding leftovers) makes this likely at the end of an index's life even without a griefer. Impact: an index cannot be revived; no funds at risk.

IHybridHubTypes.RebalanceSlashed (line 141) says 'a delivery ... short of what the fill recorded', while _isForged also slashes an intake neither open nor settled and an empty intake on a chain that recorded a delivery.

title: New units are range-checked only at settlement, after the executor has delivered
description: acceptRebalance stores _fillUnits as uint256 (line 245); settleRebalance narrows them with SafeCast.toUint96 (line 315). A unit past uint96 (reachable only after about 690 full-band raises of one component, AGENTS.md) would let the fill be accepted and delivered and then make every settlement revert, ending in a bond burn by anyone after the grace. Stage A narrows in the same transaction as the fill, so nothing is lost there.

title: Spec says claims wait 'at most the delivery window and its grace'; nothing ends an accepted fill unless someone fails it
description: settleRebalance has no deadline and failRebalance is only permitted (not automatic) after deadline + GRACE, so an accepted fill, and with it the RebalanceInProgress wait on claimOrder and acceptMigration, lasts until someone calls failRebalance or settles. The bound is real only if a minter or keeper acts; the spec states it as automatic.

title: `vaultProposal(id)` NatSpec says it is empty when nothing is pending, but an expired proposal keeps its values, and there is no pending view as DA-16 added for the other proposals
description: `vaultProposal(id)` is documented as returning "an empty one if none is pending".
