(3) FinalityVerifier: add 'error ZeroValue();' and use it at 77. (4) IXindexVault 294: '/// @notice Anyone, while neither frozen nor stalled, into a registered index, within the cap and before the intake's deadline. Deposits the native coin sent into intake `intakeId` of `index`.'

title: RlpReader accepts non-canonical RLP; safe only while every decoded buffer is hash-authenticated
description: `_decode` accepts a single byte < 0x80 wrapped as a string, long forms for short payloads and leading zeros in long lengths: `0x05`, `0x8105`, `0xb80105` and `0xb9000105` all decode to the string 0x05, and `0xc0` and `0xf800` both to the empty list (checked by emulating `_decode`). Today every decoded buffer is authenticated by a hash of its exact bytes (BNB headers by the voted block hash, trie nodes by keccak from the root, receipts through the receipts trie), so no ambiguity is reachable. The library's NatSpec says 'a malformed encoding reverts' without stating that non-canonical encodings do not, so a future use on bytes authenticated another way (a signature over a re-encoding, a value compared after decoding, a length-sensitive check) would inherit the ambiguity silently.
proposedFix: RlpReader.sol L4-6: add to the @notice: 'It does not enforce canonical encoding (a byte below 0x80 may come as a one-byte string, a long form may carry a short length or leading zeros): use it only on bytes authenticated by a hash of exactly those bytes.' Or enforce canonical form in `_decode`: revert when `prefix == 0x81 && payload byte < 0x80`, when a long form's length < 56, or when its first length byte is zero.

title: StellarStateVerifier lacks its siblings' defence-in-depth checks: no future-time refusal and no exact public-values length
description: The Sui, Aptos and NEAR verifiers refuse a signed time after the current block ('nor date a state ahead of Ethereum': SuiStateVerifier.sol:234, AptosStateVerifier.sol:113,156, NearStateVerifier.sol:125). Aptos and NEAR also refuse public values of any length but the exact one (AptosStateVerifier.sol:104,146; NearStateVerifier.sol:110). StellarStateVerifier does neither: a closeTime ahead of block.timestamp is returned as is to the hub, which compares it with deadlines (HybridHubStorage.sol:273), and abi.decode ignores trailing words. With an honest quorum and the current program, neither is exploitable, since stellar-core's 60-second slip bounds close times and SP1 binds the exact bytes. It is a drift between sibling verifiers that makes a future program change land silently.
proposedFix:
src/verifiers/StellarStateVerifier.sol after line 74:
```solidity
if (p.publicValues.length != 6 * 32) revert BadPublicValues();
```
After line 81:
```solidity
if (v.closeTime > block.timestamp) revert InTheFuture(v.closeTime);
```
Declare `BadPublicValues()` and `InTheFuture(uint256)` in IStellarStateVerifier, with unit tests hitting each error.

title: AptosStateVerifier says the trusted set's lag bounds the attested state's age; it does not, and Aptos and NEAR prove attests of any age
description: The comment says the 1-day bound on the trusted set 'also bounds the state's age from below, for a reader that takes an old state as evidence'. The statement proves any transaction at or before the signed ledger info's version (proofs/aptos/statement/src/lib.rs:385-389: only `t.version > ledger_version` is refused), through an accumulator over all history. So an attest from any time in the past verifies under a fresh ledger info. Likewise, NEAR heads never expire (NearStateVerifier.sol:186 checks only that a head is recorded), and any block under a head's block_merkle_root is provable. Sui is the only one bounded, to the current epoch. The returned timestamp is the vault's own, so the hub's `time <= notBefore` (HybridHubStorage.sol:273) is the actual bound. A reader trusting the comment could skip its own lower bound.
proposedFix: src/verifiers/AptosStateVerifier.sol lines 152-154, replace the last sentence with: "It does not bound the attested state's age: the accumulator proves any transaction at or before the ledger info's version, so the returned time, the vault's own, is the only bound, and a reader must compare it with its own deadline." Add the same caveat to NearStateVerifier.verifySlots' @dev (line 148): "Heads never expire: an attest of any age under a recorded head verifies."

title: SuiStateVerifier proves only checkpoints of the epoch in force, so the permissionless update at each epoch end invalidates every proof in flight
description: `_verify` requires s.epoch == epoch. Anyone may call `update` once the end-of-epoch checkpoint is certified, and from then on no checkpoint of the old epoch verifies. A hub transaction carrying a proof of an attest from the last part of epoch E (settleRebalance, settleOrder, evidence) can be front-run by `update` and revert; the prover must re-run `attest` in E+1 and rebuild the proof. AptosStateVerifier keeps every trusted set for a day for exactly this reason ('so it outlives the updates made while it is in flight', AptosStateVerifier.sol:28-29). This is a liveness nuisance with no loss, since re-attesting is cheap. Near the hub's 6-hour GRACE deadlines, though, it is one more way to delay a settlement.
proposedFix:
src/verifiers/SuiStateVerifier.sol:
- add `bytes32 public previousCommitteeHash;` and `uint64 public previousEpochStartMs;`
- in `update`, before overwriting (line 126): `previousCommitteeHash = committeeHash; previousEpochStartMs = epochStartMs;`
- add a `_verifyPrevious` path, used only by verifySlots, that accepts `s.epoch == epoch - 1` under previousCommitteeHash, with the same TooOld check against previousEpochStartMs.
Alternatively, document the behaviour in ISuiStateVerifier.verifySlots.

title: Interface documentation drift: ISuiStateVerifier names a non-existent committeeHash(keys, powers); INearStateVerifier omits SP1_VERIFIER and PROGRAM_KEY
description: ISuiStateVerifier.sol:130 says the committee hash is `committeeHash(keys, powers)`. The function is `hashCommittee(keys, powers)`; `committeeHash` is the storage getter, which takes no arguments. NearStateVerifier exposes `SP1_VERIFIER` and `PROGRAM_KEY` as public immutables with no NatSpec and no `@inheritdoc`, and INearStateVerifier does not declare them. IAptosStateVerifier and IStellarStateVerifier both declare them, so an integrator or deployment check written against the interface cannot read NEAR's program key.

title: Staleness boundary is inclusive: a proof exactly MAX_LAG after its anchor is still accepted
description: Each check is `if (block.timestamp > anchor + MAX_LAG) revert TooOld`, so at block.timestamp == anchor + MAX_LAG the stale set is still accepted (test_update_stopsForGoodADayBehind, test/NearStateVerifier.t.sol:226-227, pins it). The domain rule wants the staleness edge to count as stale. The effect is one second; Sui (ms / 1000), Aptos (µs / 1e6) and NEAR (ns / 1e9) also floor the anchor, which adds up to one more second. This is a repo-wide convention, shared by the BNB, TRON, CometBFT and VeChain verifiers.
proposedFix: In each listed line, `>` -> `>=`, for example in SuiStateVerifier.sol:224: `if (block.timestamp >= start / MS + MAX_LAG) revert TooOld(start);`. Update the boundary tests (for example NearStateVerifier.t.sol:226-227 to warp to `ends - 1`). Apply it consistently across every verifier, or record the inclusive edge as deliberate in AGENTS.md.

title: DeployStateVerifier's header, NatSpec and AGENTS.md list only the first two or four chains' review helpers and entry points
description: The contract header says the owner and guardian check the verifier 'with `checkBnb` or `checkTron`' (lines 26-28) although checkSui, checkInjective, checkVeChain and checkAptos exist and checkNear/checkStellar do not; `error UnknownChain` is documented as 'none of bnb, tron, near and stellar' (line 113) although run() accepts eight chains; AGENTS.md ('Scripts') names only `DeployStateVerifier.deployBnb` and `deployTron`; the abi list is current. A future session reading AGENTS.md would not know the other six entry points or that two have no review helper (see A7-02).
proposedFix: Update the header and the `UnknownChain` NatSpec to list all eight STATE_CHAIN values and every check helper (and say which chains have none), and AGENTS.md 'Scripts' to `deployBnb`, `deployTron`, `deployNear`, `deployStellar`, `deploySui`, `deployInjective`, `deployVeChain` and `deployAptos`.

title: Derived constants (verifier identities, registry ids, epoch length) are copied across Solidity, two JS tools and mocks, with no re-derivation test in the main suite
description: RISC_ZERO_SELECTOR 0x73c457ba and SP1_VERIFIER_HASH 0x0e78f4db... gate every verifier check (and A7-01's fix). They are repeated in DeployVault/ScriptUtils, tron/deploy.mjs 52-56, vechain/deploy.mjs 51-55, test/mocks/MockSP1Verifier.sol:23, MockRiscZeroVerifier.sol:21, crates/xindex-core/src/sp1.rs:17 and vechain/deploy-test.mjs, and the main suite checks them only against mocks that copy the literal. I recomputed them and they are correct: deploying the vendored RiscZeroGroth16Verifier with ControlID.CONTROL_ROOT/BN254_CONTROL_ID yields SELECTOR 0x73c457ba and VERSION 3.0.0; the vendored SP1VerifierGroth16 returns VERIFIER_HASH 0x0e78f4db7a67... and VERSION v6.0.0; the registry ids NEAR_MAINNET 339552387624818629, NEAR_TESTNET, STELLAR_PUBNET 839718837228939926, STELLAR_TESTNET, SUI_*, APTOS_* equal the first 8 bytes of keccak256 of their CAIP-2 names, the Stellar network ids equal sha256 of the passphrases, and the beacon genesis times 1606824023 (2020-12-01 12:00:23 UTC) and 1655733600 (2022-06-20 14:00 UTC) are the real ones. But test/Scripts.t.sol recomputes the NEAR and Stellar testnet ids (2327-2328) and both Sui and Aptos ids (2470-2471, 2580-2581), while NEAR_MAINNET and STELLAR_PUBNET are compared only with a bare literal (2315, 2324); EPOCH_SECONDS=384 and VERIFIER_MAX_LAG are private copies (the MAX_LAG copy is cross-checked at test line 1539, EPOCH_SECONDS is not); the JS copies have no cross-check.
proposedFix: Add to test/Scripts.t.sol: `function test_theIdentityConstantsAreRederived() public { DeployStateVerifier s = new DeployStateVerifier(); assertEq(s.NEAR_MAINNET(), uint64(bytes8(keccak256("near:mainnet")))); assertEq(s.STELLAR_PUBNET(), uint64(bytes8(keccak256("stellar:pubnet")))); assertTrue(vm.contains(vm.readFile("prototype/evm/src/sp1/SP1VerifierGroth16.sol"), vm.toString(ScriptUtils.SP1_VERIFIER_HASH))); RiscZeroGroth16Verifier v = new RiscZeroGroth16Verifier(ControlID.CONTROL_ROOT, ControlID.BN254_CONTROL_ID); assertEq(v.SELECTOR(), new DeployVault().RISC_ZERO_SELECTOR()); assertEq(v.VERSION(), new DeployVault().RISC_ZERO_VERSION()); }` (needs the remapping `openzeppelin/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/` for vendor/risc0-ethereum), and a Repo.t.sol check that the JS files' literals equal the Solidity ones by reading the three files.

title: CI does not deny compiler warnings although the definition of done says forge build must be clean
description: AGENTS.md item 2: 'forge build clean, including forge lint (zero warnings and notes)'. CI runs `forge build --sizes`, which succeeds with solc warnings; only `forge lint -D notes` is strict (lines 72-76). Today the tree is clean (I built 211 files in a scratch copy: no warnings), so this is a latent gap: a shadowing, unused-variable or unreachable-code warning would merge.
proposedFix: .github/workflows/test.yml line 70: `run: forge build --sizes --deny warnings` (forge 1.8.1 supports `-D, --deny <never|warnings|notes>`).

title: foundry.toml grants every script and test read access to the whole project root, .env included
description: `fs_permissions = [{ access = "read", path = "./" }]` applies to forge script runs as well as tests. Repo.t.sol needs foundry.toml, .github, abi, out, CLAUDE.md, .gitmodules, .env.example, README and src; DeployStateVerifier needs an anchor file. A script (or a future test or dependency) can vm.readFile('.env') (the RPC URL and Etherscan key) or the gitignored broadcast/ records. Not exploitable today (first-party code only).
proposedFix: Narrow to the directories used: `fs_permissions = [{ access = "read", path = "./test" }, { access = "read", path = "./abi" }, { access = "read", path = "./out" }, { access = "read", path = "./src" }, { access = "read", path = "./.github" }, { access = "read", path = "./foundry.toml" }, ...]` and have operators keep anchor files under a dedicated `./anchors/` read path; keep `.env` out of the list.

title: Deploy and DeployVault take the 'broadcasting key' from msg.sender in the role checks but from vm.readCallers() for the nonce
description: checkGuardian (Deploy 224-237) and DeployVault.checkRoles (206-214) compare against msg.sender; deploy() reads the real broadcaster with vm.readCallers() only to predict the factory address (109-112), and its own comment notes 'the script's own msg.sender differs in tests'. Two sources of truth for one concept: if a run ever has msg.sender != broadcaster (several signers, vm.startBroadcast(address), a future Foundry change) the 'broadcaster holds no role' and 'broadcaster is not a Safe signer' checks (SA-06) are evaluated for the wrong account and pass silently. I checked Foundry 1.8.1: with one --keystore and no --sender, msg.sender equals the signer, so the documented commands are fine today.
proposedFix: Pass the broadcaster explicitly: `checkGuardian(address owner, address guardian, address broadcaster)` and in deploy() derive it once (`vm.startBroadcast(); (, address broadcaster,) = vm.readCallers(); vm.stopBroadcast();` before the checks, or require `--sender` and read it with `vm.envAddress('DEPLOYER')`), and assert msg.sender == broadcaster when running on chain 1.

title: Launch supplies are dated 2026-09-22 and nothing makes them be refreshed before the first mainnet listing
description: The first listing sets each component's reference supply from `defaultMainnetList()` (CoinGecko, 2026-09-22) and cannot afterwards move more than 0.5% a week; README:473-476 says to 'check its figure while it can still be cancelled', but the Deploy runbook (README 636-785) has no step to refresh the four constants before `LISTING_MODE=safe WHITELIST=default LIST=all`, and test_CRL08_theDefaultListIsTheReleaseRecord pins the old figures, so a launch weeks later would list stale figures and the test would have to be edited by hand. AGENTS.md says every reference supply carries its source and date 'beside it'; the dates sit in one block comment above the four constants (LINK and UNI circulating supplies change by unlocks, BTC about 0.8% a year).
proposedFix: Add a dated source comment on each constant (`uint256 internal constant LINK_SUPPLY = 748_099_970e18; // CoinGecko circulating, 2026-09-22`), add a README Deploy step 'refresh MainnetAddresses supplies from their sources the day before the launch listing and update test_CRL08', and add a test that fails if `block.timestamp` exceeds the newest supply date by more than 30 days when run against a fork.

title: TRON deploy tool depends on caret-ranged npm packages and is installed with `npm install`; the keystore password may sit in a file
description: tron/package.json ranges tronweb ^6.0.0 and viem ^2.23.0 while vechain/package.json pins @vechain/sdk-core 2.1.0 exactly; both have lockfiles with integrity hashes and no install scripts (checked), but tron/README.md and vechain/README.md tell operators to run `npm install`, which can rewrite the lock, on the machine that decrypts the deployer keystore. `--password-file` keeps the password on disk beside the keystore, which is a raw key in effect (AGENTS.md: 'never use raw private keys').
proposedFix: Pin exact versions in tron/package.json, document `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in both READMEs, and have deploy.mjs refuse a --password-file that is group/world readable (`statSync(file).mode & 0o077`).

title: ConfigureWhitelist's 'USDC/USDT are never components' check compares against mainnet addresses only
description: _followsPolicy refuses a component equal to MainnetAddresses.USDC or USDT (chain-1 constants). Off mainnet the mint currencies are whatever USDC/USDT env values Deploy was given (README:879-884 uses tUSDC), so a testnet WHITELIST can list the deployment's own mint currency as a component, violating AGENTS.md ('Do not whitelist USDC/USDT as components in scripts').
proposedFix: Read the deployment's currencies from the environment as Deploy does: `address u = vm.envOr("USDC", MainnetAddresses.USDC); address t = vm.envOr("USDT", MainnetAddresses.USDT); if (token == u || token == t || token == MainnetAddresses.USDC || token == MainnetAddresses.USDT) { ... skipped ... }`, with a test using tUSDC.

title: TRON and VeChain tools default unset NATIVE_CAP, NATIVE_FLOOR and ANCHOR_EPOCH to 0 where DeployVault refuses
description: DeployVault.run reads these with vm.envUint, which reverts when unset; paramsFromEnv in tron/deploy.mjs (102-106) and vechain/deploy.mjs (110-114) default them to '0'. A missing VAULT_NATIVE_CAP therefore passes check (floor 0 <= cap 0) and deploys a vault whose native cap is 0, which refuses every deposit (cap[NATIVE]=0, XindexVault.sol:193) until a CAP_UPDATE through the factory (LISTING_DELAY) raises it. An unset epoch fails closed (AnchorTooOld). The 'twin' differs in exactly the way the doc says it does not (README: 'the same checks').
proposedFix: In both paramsFromEnv: `const need = (k) => { if (env[k] === undefined) throw new Refused('Required', k); return BigInt(env[k]); }` for VAULT_ANCHOR_EPOCH, VAULT_NATIVE_CAP and VAULT_NATIVE_FLOOR (and require nativeCap > 0 in check on both sides), with a deploy-test case for each missing variable.

title: min_payout covers only an empty recipient; a rent-paying legacy recipient fails the whole delivery
description: SOL-5's fix lets a payout wait while `recipient.lamports() == 0` and the payout is below the zero-data rent minimum. Agave's rent-state rule allows a still rent-paying account only if its lamports do not rise (RentPaying to RentPaying requires post <= pre). So a payout that leaves a pre-existing rent-paying account still below exemption fails the transaction. That makes `deliver_burn` itself revert, rather than recording the debt as owed. The same applies to a recipient with data whose balance sits below its own rent minimum. The burn is only delayed, since anyone can top the recipient up to exemption. Such accounts are rare.

title: Spec section 7 says the vault calls each verifier 'with the verifier's state account at a fixed address'; the real P1/P2 take a per-headers-root range PDA and an optional buffer
description: Spec section 7 (line 786) says each verifier's verify_event runs 'with the verifier's state account at a fixed address of its own'. The production verifiers' verify_event and verify_checkpoint take `[range]` or `[range, buffer]` (ethereum-verifier/src/lib.rs:17-31, 268-289). The range is the PDA ["range", headersRoot], which differs per update. Only the stub reads a fixed 'verifier' state account. A relayer implementer reading the spec would pass the wrong account.
proposedFix: design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-b-spec.md:786. BEFORE: 'which must succeed, with the verifier's state account at a fixed address of its own.' AFTER: 'which must succeed, with the verifier's own accounts: for P1 and P2 the range account ["range", headersRoot] the proof's headers root names, then a loader buffer when the proof is staged; for the testnet stub its state at ["verifier"] and its relayer.'

title: begin_snapshot adds a storage entry with no deposit or charge, drawing on whatever balance the vault has beyond its storage stake; storage callers pay is never released
description: Every other method that grows storage is #[payable] and calls `charge`. `begin_snapshot` (non-payable) inserts `slots[u256(25)]` (lines 619-620), about 105 bytes, i.e. about 0.001 NEAR of storage stake, paid from the vault's own balance; `apply_change(FREEZER_CHANGE)` can also lengthen the freezer AccountId inside STATE (up to about 22 bytes). The vault's liquid balance beyond its stake is only the NEP-616 creation deposit's surplus plus gas rewards: `charge` makes callers pay exactly their growth, so no slack accrues from them. If the creation deposit was close to the minimum, `begin_snapshot` fails with LackBalanceForState and the 180-day last-resort exit is blocked. Unlikely (the sandbox deploys with 5 NEAR), but the exit is the path that must never fail. Related: storage depositors and relayers pay for (owed, used, intakes, deposits entries) is never freed (no removal anywhere), which near/README.md does not say (the Solana twin records it as SOL-8).
proposedFix: near/contracts/xindex-vault/src/lib.rs line 610-611: `#[payable] pub fn begin_snapshot(&mut self) { let before = env::storage_usage(); ... self.charge(before, 0); }` (callers then fund the 0.001 NEAR), or document a minimum creation deposit in near/README.md 'No owner, no key' step 2. Add one README sentence: 'storage paid is permanent; nothing is ever deleted'.

title: decode_message truncates the body length with `as usize`, so on 32-bit targets (NEAR and Soroban Wasm) a non-canonical length word is accepted
description: `let len = to_u64(word(p, 8)?)? as usize;` keeps only the low 32 bits on wasm32. A payload whose length word is 2^32 + n with n body bytes decodes as length n, although the doc says the canonical encoding only is accepted and Solidity's `abi.decode` would revert on it. `padded(len)` can also wrap in non-overflow-checked builds for a length within 31 of usize::MAX (rejected anyway by the zero-tail check, as `start + len` wraps into the length word). Not exploitable today: a message is identified by keccak256(payload) and must match a log the hub or factory emitted, which always writes canonical lengths. It matters only as a broken stated invariant ('one message must have one encoding').

title: Stale comment in crates/xindex-core/Cargo.toml: NEAR and Stellar are described as next
description: The comment reads 'each chain's workspace (Solana's now, NEAR's and Stellar's next) takes this crate as a path dependency', but near/ and stellar/ are built and depend on it (near/contracts/xindex-vault/Cargo.toml:16, stellar/Cargo.toml:16).
proposedFix: crates/xindex-core/Cargo.toml lines 26-28: replace '(Solana's now, NEAR's and Stellar's next)' with '(Solana's, NEAR's and Stellar's)'.

title: u64 chain ids above 2^53 are serialized as JSON numbers in the `config` view, which JavaScript clients misread
description: `ConfigView.chain_id` (and `InitConfig.chain_id`) is a plain u64. NEAR mainnet's registry id is 339552387624818629 and testnet's 4078699518750379172, both above 2^53-1, so `JSON.parse` of the `config` view in near-api-js (the web app, relayers) yields 339552387624818620 / ...800. A client that takes the chain id from that view to build a holder's EIP-712 snapshot claim digest (snapshot::claim_digest names the chain id) signs a digest for the wrong chain; the vault then refuses it (BadSignature, fail-closed) at the very exit where holders have no other path. near-sdk's convention for large u64 is `json_types::U64`.
proposedFix: types.rs: `pub chain_id: near_sdk::json_types::U64` in ConfigView (line 266) (and InitConfig line 193 with `.0` at the use sites in lib.rs build), and document that clients must use the string.

title: is_implicit, the recovery-proposer 'not a single-key account' guard, does not know nearcore's newer account family (`0u` universal accounts)
description: `Vault::build` refuses a recovery proposer only if `is_implicit` (64 lowercase hex, or `0x` + 40 hex). nearcore master (runtime/runtime/src/actions.rs, `AccountType::UniversalAccount`, ids of the form `0u...`, gated by the `universal_accounts` wasm-config flag) adds an account family whose id commits to a state init that can install access keys and code; whether such an account is one key's is a property of its state init, which a contract cannot read. A `0u` recovery proposer therefore passes the check that exists to stop a single-key proposer, and the README's off-chain checks (view_code hash, view_access_key_list, confirmations, README lines 112-118) are the only remaining guard. I could not confirm the feature is live on mainnet by the deployment date; the protocol-level text is in nearcore master only. Low impact: the proposer can only propose a successor during a 180-day-bounded stall, with a 30-day review and two vetoes.
proposedFix: near/contracts/xindex-vault/src/types.rs is_implicit: also return true for any id that starts with `0u` (universal accounts), and add `|| s.starts_with("0u")`; keep README lines 112-118 as the real check. Add the id family to the README sentence 'The vault refuses an implicit account (ed25519 or ETH-implicit)'.

title: proofs/stellar README example passes an argument the CLI ignores
description: README line 53 runs `./target/release/stellar-proof execute --mainnet statement/fixtures/mainnet.json 14`. `script/src/main.rs` (usage block, lines 3-9, and `execute`, line 126) defines the optional third argument as `--all` only (`all = args.get(2) == Some("--all")`), so `14` is silently ignored and the run uses the minimal 14-signature set by default. The example reads as if 14 selected the signature count.
proposedFix: proofs/stellar/README.md:53: `./target/release/stellar-proof execute --mainnet statement/fixtures/mainnet.json            # the fewest signatures that satisfy Tier 1 (14)` and add `--all` for every Tier 1 signature (30).

title: Light-client `epoch` is deployer-declared and unbounded above, so LG-4's lag can be defeated until the first update (both Move vaults); `create` checks only the `system` label, never the program key
description: `light_client::new/create` stores the caller's `epoch`, `genesis_time`, `key` and `anchor` without relating `epoch` to the clock. `lag_ends = genesis_time + epoch*384 + MAX_LAG` (saturating to u64::MAX), and `vault::create` only requires `now <= lag_ends`. A client created with an `epoch` in the future (typo or hostile deployer) passes every on-chain check and never lag-stops until its first proven `update` overwrites `lc.epoch` from the statement; LG-4 ('P1 and P2 stop for good a day behind') is therefore not enforced for that window. Likewise `system` (1/2) is just a label: `vault::create` accepts any `key` (a trivial or testnet program key) as 'P1' or 'P2'; only the off-chain checklist (README) pins SP1 vkey / RISC Zero image id. The EVM `FinalityVerifier` constructor has the same property, so this is parity, not a regression; it is a hazard because the Move `create` advertises that it 'refuses what DeployVault refuses where Move can see it' and an epoch bound IS something Move can see.
proposedFix: Add a public view `epoch_start(lc) = genesis_time + epoch*384` to both light_client modules and, in both vault::create functions, require the anchor's epoch to have begun. sui/sources/vault.move after line 383: `assert!(light_client::epoch_start(p1) <= now && light_client::epoch_start(p2) <= now, EAnchorTooOld);` ; aptos/sources/vault.move after line 448: same with addresses. light_client.move: `public fun epoch_start(lc: &LightClient): u64 { lc.genesis_time + lc.epoch * SECONDS_PER_EPOCH }` (use u128 as lag_ends does). Add a test that a client created with epoch = 2^40 is refused.

title: Rotated and successor light-client pairs skip the genesis, lag and role checks `create` applies (check_pair only tests distinct ids and distinct system labels)
description: `create` requires p1 to be an SP1 client, p2 a RISC Zero client, both with the source chain's beacon genesis and both still within their lag. `apply_rotation` / `apply(VERIFIER_ROTATION)` and `propose_successor` call only `check_pair`, which asserts different ids and different `system` labels, so (a) p1 may be the RISC Zero client and p2 the SP1 one, (b) a pair with a different `genesis_time` (e.g. a Sepolia-genesis client on a mainnet vault) is accepted, and (c) a pair whose lag already expired (a client that can never `update` again, so the vault stalls) is accepted by a rotation. A rotation passes ROTATION_DELAY (30 days) at the factory and GOVERNANCE_DELAY (7 days) on the vault with the freezer's cancel, so reviewers can catch it; the EVM `_checkPair` is equally weak (code length, distinct). Inconsistent hardening between creation and replacement is the hazard: the check that matters most (the pair must be alive and on the right network) exists only on the path that is run once.
proposedFix: Factor create's pair assertions into one function and call it from create, apply_rotation/apply(VERIFIER_ROTATION) and propose_successor. Sui, replace line 926-929 `check_pair(p1, p2)` body with: `assert!(object::id(p1) != object::id(p2), EVerifiersNotDistinct); assert!(light_client::system(p1) == light_client::sp1() && light_client::system(p2) == light_client::risc_zero(), EWrongVerifier); assert!(light_client::genesis_time(p1) == genesis_of(vault) && light_client::genesis_time(p2) == genesis_of(vault), EWrongVerifier); assert!(now(clock) <= light_client::lag_ends(p1) && now(clock) <= light_client::lag_ends(p2), EAnchorTooOld);` (pass vault and clock in; `genesis_of` maps source_chain_id to ETHEREUM_GENESIS/SEPOLIA_GENESIS as create does at lines 369-376). Same in aptos/sources/vault.move lines 1071-1076.
priorArt: VLT-2 (rotation delay), FAC-1; none on the pair's fitness

title: Twin drift on the protective path: Move vaults abort a FREEZE whose body is non-empty, the EVM vault freezes regardless
description: `XindexVault._governanceMessage` freezes on any FREEZE message and never reads its body. Both Move twins add `assert!(body.is_empty(), EBadMessage)` before freezing. Today the factory sends FREEZE with an empty body (src/HybridIndexFactory.sol:132) so the drift is inert, but the freeze is the one message designed to pass on a single proof, and a future factory/hub version that adds a field (a reason code, a chain id) would freeze EVM vaults and silently fail to freeze Sui and Aptos vaults, with the delivery aborting rather than freezing. Fail-closed on input means the protective message should be the most permissive to parse. Related smaller drifts (all inert with today's senders): Move requires cap/burn/migration/rotation bodies to be exactly N words where Solidity's abi.decode tolerates trailing bytes; Move aborts a BURN or CAP_UPDATE naming a non-native token (ENotNative) where the EVM vault records an unpayable owed entry / a cap. AGENTS.md's twin rule ('a change to a vault's rule or a message goes into each') has no list of intended differences to check these against.
proposedFix: sui/sources/vault.move line 1120 and aptos/sources/vault.move line 1283: delete `assert!(body.is_empty(), EBadMessage);` (keep EBadMessage for the other kinds), so a FREEZE freezes whatever it carries, as XindexVault does. Add a one-line test per twin: a FREEZE payload with a 32-byte body freezes. In AGENTS.md 'Sui, Aptos, Injective and VeChain' add a sentence listing the intended Move strictness (exact body words, native token only).
priorArt: VLT-4, LG-3 (what a one-proof freeze may do)

title: Aptos P1/P2 `update` feasibility rests on an estimated, unmeasured gas figure (the unit-test runner meters nothing)
description: The README states that the Aptos unit-test runner meters no gas, so every figure is derived from coverage maps, an opcode price table and, for the BN254 natives, schedule formulas with `multi_scalar_mul` priced at an upper bound; 'Real figures need a simulation'. The only hard limit quoted is 9,200 execution gas units per transaction against ~2,000 for an `update`. The whole vault depends on someone calling `update` on both light clients at least daily (LG-4); if the real cost of four pairings plus thirteen subgroup-checked point reads exceeded the cap, P1 and P2 could never advance, the vault would stall after 7 days and holders would wait 180 more days for the snapshot exit. ARCHITECTURE.md carries the same 'about 2,000 gas units an update, estimated' with the caveat. Not a defect in the code, but a liveness assumption with a ~4.6x margin that has not been measured, on a path where failure is slow and costly.
proposedFix: Before the registry lists an Aptos vault, require a measured figure: run `aptos move publish` + `update` on a local/test network (outside this repo's no-CLI rule, by the deployer) or `aptos move simulate` against testnet with a real SP1/RISC Zero fixture, and record the `gas_used` of `light_client::update` for P1 and P2 and of `deliver` in aptos/README.md replacing the estimates. Add the measured numbers to the deployment checklist at README step 5.

title: Margin reasoning omits consolidations completing after the anchor; 'over twice the drift below 50M ETH' is false
description: The spec (section 10, 'The margin') and the comment on MARGIN_PER_EPOCH_GWEI (proofs/finality/src/statement.rs:23-27) bound the records' drift per epoch by the balance churn plus 256 ETH (about 775 ETH at 34M ETH staked) and claim the 2,048 ETH margin is over twice that below about 50M ETH (the LG-I1 fix). It misses a term: an Electra consolidation consumes its churn when requested, but the source's balance reaches the target only when the source becomes withdrawable, MIN_VALIDATOR_WITHDRAWABILITY_DELAY (256 epochs) after its exit (process_pending_consolidations, then process_effective_balance_updates). So within a proof's day, targets the anchor's records show at their old effective balance can each gain up to ~2,016 ETH of active stake with no churn at that moment, at a rate up to the consolidation churn (balance churn - 256 ETH) of their exit epochs. The worst-case drift is then about twice the balance churn: ~1,038 ETH/epoch at 34M (margin 1.97x, not 'over twice'), ~1,526 at 50M, and it reaches the margin at ~67M ETH staked (by the spec's own X+Y accounting; ~80M by X + 2/3 Y). Compounding validators' reward-driven effective-balance growth (a few ETH per epoch network-wide) is likewise uncounted. No soundness break at today's stake; the documented safety factor is overstated.
proposedFix: design/2026-09-30-v4-stage-b-spec.md:1040-1052 and proofs/finality/src/statement.rs:23-27: add the bullet '- consolidations add stake to their targets 256 epochs after the churn they took, so a day can see the targets of earlier requests grow by up to the consolidation churn an epoch, which no record shows' and change the bound to 'about twice the balance churn an epoch: about 1,040 ETH at 34M ETH staked; the 2,048 ETH margin covers it up to about 67M ETH'. Optionally raise MARGIN_PER_EPOCH_GWEI or scale it with the recorded total (e.g. 2 * max(128 ETH, total/65,536) + 256 ETH, with headroom) so the bound holds at any stake.
priorArt: LG-I1 (fixed by documentation; this refines it)

title: P1 and P2 'two different verifiers' is enforced as two different addresses only
description: AGENTS.md: 'P1 and P2 must always be two different verifiers' (two zkVMs from different teams, so one broken proof system cannot forge alone). On chain this is only `a != b` plus code presence (XindexVault._checkPair, :770-774; HybridIndexFactory.proposeRotation :182 compares the two bytes32). A VERIFIER_ROTATION or a recovery successor naming two EthereumFinalityVerifier instances (both SP1, possibly the same PROGRAM_KEY), or two RiscZero ones, passes every check, after which one broken system forges every two-proof message. The Solana vault likewise only requires two distinct, immutable program ids (setup.rs/governance.rs/recovery.rs `require_keys_neq!`), and nothing distinguishes an `ethereum-verifier` deployment from a `risc0-verifier` one. The rotation is behind ROTATION_DELAY + GOVERNANCE_DELAY with the freezer's cancel and the successor behind a 30-day review, so this is a trust-and-review hazard, not an exploit; it is a convention-vs-enforcement gap.
proposedFix: Give each verifier a fixed system tag and check it: add `function PROOF_SYSTEM() external pure returns (bytes32)` to IEthereumEventVerifier (EthereumFinalityVerifier returns keccak256("SP1"), RiscZeroFinalityVerifier keccak256("RISC0"), each state verifier its own), and in XindexVault._checkPair (:770-774) add `if (IEthereumEventVerifier(a).PROOF_SYSTEM() == IEthereumEventVerifier(b).PROOF_SYSTEM()) revert VerifiersNotDistinct();`. Self-reported, so it guards against mistakes rather than a malicious owner, which the delays already cover; mirror on Solana by reading each program's state account layout/tag.

title: The first anchor's epoch is a second, unbound source of truth beside the anchor hash
description: The constructor takes `initialAnchor` (keccak of epoch, validatorsRoot, execHash, execNumber) and `initialEpoch` separately and stores both (:76-81); DeployVault reads them from two env vars (VAULT_ANCHOR, VAULT_ANCHOR_EPOCH, script/DeployVault.s.sol:115-116) and checks the lag only against the given epoch (:176-177); Solana's `initialize` does the same (solana/programs/ethereum-verifier/src/lib.rs:295-327). Nothing ties the stored epoch to the one inside the hash. A larger initialEpoch moves the first lagEnds() later, letting the deployer's (possibly old) anchor be advanced once after LG-4's day has passed; a smaller one stops the verifier early. Only the listing-delay review catches the mismatch.
proposedFix: Take the preimage and hash it on chain: `constructor(uint64 initialEpoch, bytes32 validatorsRoot, bytes32 execHash, uint64 execNumber, uint256 genesisTime)` with `anchor = keccak256(abi.encode(initialEpoch, validatorsRoot, execHash, execNumber)); anchorEpoch = initialEpoch;` (the statement's Anchor::hash encoding, proofs/finality/src/statement.rs:43-51), and have DeployVault and `p1-input check-state` pass the four fields instead of the hash; same for Solana `initialize` data.

title: Network separation rests only on an unchecked program key / image id; the public values never name the network
description: Mainnet vs Sepolia is fixed only by which program the key/image id names (proofs/finality/src/beacon.rs:14-56); the public values and the anchor hash (statement.rs:43-51) carry no network id or genesis validators root. DeployVault takes VAULT_P1_KEY and VAULT_P2_IMAGE_ID as free inputs and checks only that they are non-zero (:173-174), while VAULT_SOURCE_CHAIN_ID picks the genesis time (:184-187). A Sepolia key with a mainnet anchor cannot advance (registry mismatch: liveness only), but a Sepolia key with a Sepolia anchor under VAULT_SOURCE_CHAIN_ID=1 gives a vault that follows Sepolia's finality as if it were Ethereum's; only the anchor's listing-delay review stands between. ScriptUtils.isSp1Verifier and checkVerifiers (script/ScriptUtils.sol:46-49, DeployVault.s.sol:190-201) likewise identify the Groth16 verifiers by their self-reported VERIFIER_HASH/VERSION/SELECTOR views, not by code, though AGENTS.md says the script refuses 'any Groth16 verifier but the pinned SP1 and RISC Zero ones'.
proposedFix: Bind the network in the statement: include GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT in Anchor::hash (statement.rs:45-50: `keccak(&[&GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT, &word(self.epoch), ...])`) and in the deployer's/check-state anchor, so a wrong-network program or anchor can never advance; and/or pin the released mainnet and Sepolia P1 keys and P2 image ids per VAULT_SOURCE_CHAIN_ID in DeployVault.check. Pin the SP1 v6.0.0 and RISC Zero 3.0 Groth16 verifiers' runtime codehashes in checkVerifiers (EVM chains) rather than only their view answers, or reword AGENTS.md to 'that name themselves'.

title: Solana design record states 2^160 security for truncated Merkle nodes; a leader equivocating on a block id needs only a 2^80 collision
description: Section 2 says 'Nodes are 20 bytes, so a second preimage costs 2^160' and section 4 item 3 repeats '160-bit second-preimage security'. proofs/solana-state/src/block_id.rs join() hashes only left[..20] ++ right[..20], so a block id binds each FEC-set root (and each double-Merkle child) through its first 20 bytes. The party who chooses the last FEC set's contents is the slot's leader, who can search for two different FEC sets (different footers, hence different bank hashes) whose roots share their first 20 bytes: a birthday collision of about 2^80 SHA-256 evaluations, after which one block id (one notarize/finalize certificate) opens to two footers and the prover may present whichever suits. This is inherited from Agave's own shred Merkle design, not introduced here, and may be acceptable, but the record's trust section should state the 80-bit collision bound that the whole Solana state proof then inherits, instead of only the 160-bit second-preimage figure.
proposedFix: design/2026-10-03-solana-state-proof.md line 114: append ' A leader who chooses the last FEC set can instead search for a collision of two 20-byte truncated roots, about 2^80 work; the state proof inherits that bound from Agave.' and add the same sentence to section 4 item 3 and to the spec's list of trust assumptions.

title: Solana prototype: bank-hash and double-Merkle block-id compositions are checked only against vectors the same author composed from reading Agave
description: vectors.json's lattice-hash vectors are Agave's own (read out of lt_hash.rs), but 'bankHash' ('computed here with Python's hashlib, as Bank::hash_internal_state composes it, over chosen inputs') and 'blockId' ('a double Merkle root computed here') are the author's reading of the source, and bank.rs/block_id.rs were written from the same reading. The devnet fixture holds a real finalized block (blockhash, certificate) but its probes getBankHash/getAccountsLtHash/getBlockFooter returned errors, so no real bank hash or real block id (a real finalized block's id verifies the certificate on devnet but is never recomputed from shreds) ties the composition to chain data. A wrong byte order, a missing hard-fork rule or a wrong leaf layout would pass every test and fail only on first contact with the chain. The design record flags the footer framing as open; it does not flag these two as unvalidated. Prototype only, nothing depends on it yet.
proposedFix: Before the statement is written: add a fixture with one real finalized block's shreds (devnet or mainnet), recompute its block id with block_id::block_id and assert equality with the id the certificate signs (cert.rs tests already hold the certificate), and one real bank hash taken from a validator's log or snapshot manifest asserted against BankHashPreimage::hash. Record in proofs/solana-state/README or the lib.rs header that bank.rs and block_id.rs are unvalidated against chain data until then.

title: Aptos TransactionInfo::V1 layout is verified only against the statement's own encoder
description: transaction_info writes V1 as variant 1, gas_used, status, transaction_hash, event_root, state_change_hash, then Option fields in the order state_checkpoint, hot_state_checkpoint, auxiliary_info, position_state_checkpoint, then seven placeholder Options. Mainnet's fixture transaction info starts 0x00 (V0), so V0 is checked against real chain bytes, but V1 has no real vector: a_v1_transaction_info_is_written_too (tests/statement.rs 716-736) builds a V1 with the testkit, calls c.reroot() (which re-hashes with the same encoder) and verifies, which proves only self-consistency. I could not check aptos-core's V1 field order from here. If the order or arity is wrong, every `attest` proof for a transaction that Aptos stores as V1 fails with NotInAccumulator: a liveness loss for Aptos exits and slot proofs that is fail-closed, never a forgery.
proposedFix: When Aptos Labs' backups first contain a V1 TransactionInfo, add it as a mainnet fixture (generate.py) and a test that bcs::transaction_info reproduces its BCS byte for byte, as mainnet_bcs_round_trips does for V0. Until then note in proofs/aptos/README.md that V1 is untested against chain data.

title: VeChain statement never links its header chain to trusted_id; 'after the trusted block' is only a number comparison, and the docs do not say the safety argument rests wholly on the vouching quorum
description: verify() only checks linked[0].number > trusted_number, where trusted_number is read from the first four bytes of the caller's trusted_id; the headers' first parent_id is not compared with trusted_id (it cannot be: the chain may start many blocks later), and the genesis id `chain` is bound to the headers only through the transaction chain tag (one byte, verify_call line 436) and the trusted table's signer keys. Soundness is therefore exactly: more than two thirds of the trusted table's weight signed blocks that descend from the attest block (quorum over linked[at+1..]), plus honest-validators-execute-blocks. That argument is sound under the stated model and every table also needs it, but README ('a chain of headers ... all after the trusted block'), the module doc and VeChainStateVerifier's NatSpec read as if the proof chain extends the trusted block. A future edit that weakened the vouching slice (for example vouching from a different slice of the chain, or reusing signers across the attest block's own round) would not be caught by any link check.
proposedFix: proofs/vechain/statement/src/lib.rs near line 489: extend the comment to 'Not linked to trusted_id: the chain is vouched by the trusted table's quorum alone (see `attested`)', and mirror it in proofs/vechain/README.md 'The statement' and in VeChainStateVerifier's @dev block.

title: Program keys and image ids are not recorded in the repo, and the proof workspaces float on the `stable` toolchain
description: script/DeployVault.s.sol:113-114 takes VAULT_P1_KEY / VAULT_P2_IMAGE_ID from the environment (`p1 vkey`, `p2 image-id`); no committed file or test records the expected mainnet key/image id or rebuilds it, so a P1/P2 program that differs from the audited statement cannot be detected by any test (the Sepolia program key is pinned by tests/sepolia.rs). proofs/README.md:54 notes the image id depends on the build. The vault workspaces pin rustc 1.98.1 (crates/xindex-core, near, solana, stellar rust-toolchain.toml) but proofs/rust-toolchain, proofs/{aptos,cometbft,near,stellar,vechain}/rust-toolchain all say `channel = "stable"`, so native statement tests and any non-docker guest build float. Embedded verifier constants that ARE checked: SP1 selector/VK_ROOT and RISC0 CONTROL_ROOT/BN254_CONTROL_ID/SELECTOR agree between core, Sui, Aptos and DeployVault (recomputed by comparison; each is exercised by a real proof in the Rust/Move proof tests).
proposedFix: Pin proofs/rust-toolchain and the five per-workspace rust-toolchain files to the same `channel = "1.98.1"` as the vault workspaces; add proofs/EXPECTED_KEYS.md or a json (p1 vkey, p2 image id per release, from the reproducible build) and a script/test that DeployVault.deploy refuses a key not in it on chain 1.

title: abi/IHybridIndex.json omits the hub's VaultMessage event and the ERC-20/ECDSA/SafeERC20 errors the hub can raise
description: Comparing the compiled ABIs (out/ artifacts, possibly older than src/) of HybridHub, HybridHubModule and HybridHubExtension with IHybridIndex: events missing from IHybridIndex are VaultMessage (emitted by every hub send; only abi/HybridIndexFactory.json carries it, README:337-340 presents IHybridIndex as the hybrid index's ABI), Initialized and EIP712DomainChanged; errors missing include ERC20InsufficientBalance/Allowance/InvalidReceiver/Sender, ERC2612ExpiredSignature, ECDSAInvalidSignature*, ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall, SafeERC20FailedOperation, FailedCall, SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast, InvalidInitialization. The web app and relayers decoding an index's logs and reverts from this file get an undecodable log/selector. CI regenerates only what the interface declares, so the omission is stable and unflagged.
proposedFix: Either document in README:337-340 that the hub's VaultMessage event and OpenZeppelin errors come from abi/HybridIndexFactory.json / OZ, or declare them in IHybridHub (event VaultMessage(bytes32 indexed id, bytes payload); error ERC20InsufficientBalance(address,uint256,uint256); ...) and regenerate abi/IHybridIndex.json.
